routes.source_title: Hear the wider phrase
routes.visible_owner_title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar
routes.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 as before, and row 4 of the grid shows the four trigs one beat apart inside the 16-step range. Masks stays open so chapter 5 starts on the page it needs.

routes.source_title: Open Masks for chapter 5
routes.visible_owner_title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar
routes.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), tap (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4) to remove those trigs, then tap (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4) to add trigs. Keep (1,4). PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: four steps apart is one beat at 90 BPM.

routes.source_title: Loop all 16 steps
routes.visible_owner_title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar
routes.caption: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1 to 4 and is assigned to channel 1, which loops steps 1 to 4. Channel 1's Masks are Note C3 (60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, and the tempo is 90 BPM. Playback is stopped.

routes.source_title: Check the clock rate
routes.visible_owner_title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar
routes.caption: Hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4): the range is now 16 steps, one bar. On row 4, steps 5 to 16 now glow dimly because they are inside the loop (they were dark at range 4), and the trigs are still on steps 1 to 4. Then open the Clock page for the next step: turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3.

routes.source_title: Move the trigs onto the beats
routes.visible_owner_title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar
routes.caption: Select Rate (the top row of the CLOCK page; turn E2 up if it is not highlighted) and press K3. CLOCK CH01 shows Rate /1, the default sixteenth-note rate: each step lasts 1/6 s at 90 BPM and the 16 steps last 2.7 s. Nothing changes here; this confirms the rate that every timing in the course relies on.

routes.source_title: Assign pattern 1 and loop four steps
routes.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1), then tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Row 4 holds steps 1 to 16, so these are the first four steps. PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows four bright trigs at the left of row 4. Four neighbouring trigs are a deliberately plain rhythm to hear first; chapter 4 spreads them out.

routes.source_title: Enter four trigs
routes.caption: The project from chapter 2: channel 1 sends to a MIDI instrument on port 1, MIDI channel 1 (its Device page shows CC Device, MIDI channel CC1, MIDI port OUT 1), and the tempo is 90 BPM (GLOBAL FEEL shows Tempo 90). No pattern has trigs yet, nothing is assigned to a channel and playback is stopped.

routes.source_title: Set pitch, velocity and length
routes.caption: Turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 lists eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4), all X: no mask is set, so the channel has no pitch, velocity or length yet. With no step held, E2 chooses a cell and E3 sets that cell for every step of the channel.

routes.source_title: Play the loop
routes.caption: Select Note with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads C3 (it starts at X, so about 60 detents), select Vel and turn E3 right to 80 (about 80 detents), then select Len and turn E3 right to 1/2 (8 detents). NOTE MASKS CH01 now lists Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2, the defaults for every step.

routes.source_title: Open the Masks page
routes.caption: Row 4 of the channel page is the range row: hold (1,4), tap (4,4) and release (1,4) to loop only steps 1 to 4. Steps 1 to 4 stay bright, the rest go dark, and the tooltip reads Channel 1 length changed.

routes.source_title: Read the grid and norns controls
routes.caption: You start from a new, empty project: transport stopped, nothing set up, channel 1 selected. Tap Channel (3,8), the third button on the bottom row. The screen opens NOTE MASKS for CH01 with eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4) that all read X: no value is set, because a new channel has no pattern, pitch or sound yet. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because channel 1 is the channel you edit, and (3,8) is lit because it is the page you are on.

routes.source_title: Learn the three objects
routes.caption: A new, empty project is open on NOTE MASKS for channel 1 before the first course action. No mask is set.

routes.source_title: Apply D major
routes.visible_owner_title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm
routes.caption: Turn E2 to Root and turn E3 right two detents to D. SCALE SLOT 02 shows Root D, Scale Major and the line Press K3 to confirm. The change is only a draft until K3, so playback would still use C major.

routes.source_title: Draft D major
routes.visible_owner_title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm
routes.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) to open the scale page, tap scale slot 2 at (2,3), then play two passes and stop. While it plays the screen shows SCALE SLOT 02 with Root C and Scale Major. Slot 2 holds C major like slot 1, so nothing changes: the MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62 on channel 1 and 48 and 55 on channel 2. Ignore the Degree and Transpose rows on this page; they stay at I and 0.

routes.source_title: Set up scale slot 2 and check the phrase
routes.visible_owner_title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm
routes.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), play two passes and stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 60, 60, 60, 62 from the pattern's own notes, step 13 at velocity 50, and channel 2 sounding 48 and 55.

routes.source_title: Clear fixed-pitch Note masks and keep the quiet ending
routes.visible_owner_title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, C, C, C, D, from channel and step masks: Note C3 (60), Vel 80, and on step 13 Note D3 (62) at Vel 50; NOTE MASKS CH01 is open. Channel 2 plays pattern 2 (degrees 0 and 4, octave -1) as MIDI 48 and 55. The merge Strategy is still All, which changes nothing with one pattern. Scale slot 1 is C major and the tempo is 90 BPM.

routes.source_title: Write the melody into the pattern
routes.visible_owner_title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm
routes.caption: Release (13,4). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X and Vel 80 (the channel defaults); step 13's own Vel 50 only shows while you hold it.

routes.source_title: Return to C major
routes.visible_owner_title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm
routes.caption: Press K3 to apply: the Press K3 to confirm line disappears. Play two passes and stop. While it plays SCALE SLOT 02 shows Root D and the Play pad (1,8) is lit. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 62, 62, 62, 64 (the last at velocity 50) and channel 2 sounding 50 and 57: the same rhythm in D major.

routes.source_title: Open Load project
routes.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then hold K1, tap (1,1) and release K1. The title reads CH01 with no MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 unmuted: slot 1 now plays the phrase. This change is not saved.

routes.source_title: Open Save project
routes.caption: Slot 1 has channel 1 muted and slot 2 has both channels audible, each 16 steps with Repeats 1 and Song mode On. The project has not been saved under a name yet and playback is stopped.

routes.source_title: Replay the restored sections
routes.caption: Press K3 on > Load project, turn E2 to Four notes in the file list and press K3, then tap K1 to return to Mosaic and tap Channel (3,8). The title reads CH01 MUTE again: the unsaved change is gone and slot 1 is bass alone.

routes.source_title: Reload to check the saved version
routes.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn E2 to > Load project. The norns menu shows Load project selected; K2 would cancel the dialog.

routes.source_title: Save the arrangement
routes.caption: Tap K1 briefly for the norns menu, turn E1 to PARAMS and press K3, open MOSAIC and turn E2 to < Save project. The norns menu lists Pattern project management with Save project selected.

routes.source_title: Make an unsaved change
routes.caption: Press K3 on < Save project. The norns text entry screen opens with the suggested name new: press K3 on DEL to delete it, then turn E2 to each character of Four notes and press K3 to enter it, and confirm. Saving writes Four notes.ptn and Four notes.pset. Tap K1 to return to Mosaic, which still shows SLOT SETUP, SONG 01; the text entry itself is on the norns menu, not on this frame.

routes.source_title: Optional: clear the ending’s exceptions
routes.caption: Play two passes and stop. The MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62 again, and step 13 is still at velocity 50.

routes.source_title: Optional: change the default beneath the ending
routes.caption: After you release (13,4) the screen shows the channel default Vel 80 again. Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows notes 60, 60, 60 at velocity 80 and note 62 at velocity 50.

routes.source_title: Optional: return the default to C
routes.caption: Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows 67, 67, 67 on steps 1, 5 and 9 and 62 at velocity 50 on step 13: you hear G, G, G, D because step 13 keeps its own note.

routes.source_title: Raise the last note
routes.caption: Hold (13,4), the fourth trig, and keep holding it. The title row changes to CH01 ST13: from now the screen edits step 13 only, and its Note still reads C3 because step 13 has no exception yet.

routes.source_title: Select the last beat
routes.caption: With no step held, turn E2 to Note. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3 in the highlighted cell. With no step number in the title row, C3 is the default for every step of the channel; no step has a mask of its own yet.

routes.source_title: Optional: rebuild the ending
routes.caption: Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows 60 at velocity 80 on all four steps.

routes.source_title: Hear the new ending
routes.caption: Release (13,4). The title row returns to CH01 and Note shows the channel default C3 again. Step 13 still keeps D3: hold (13,4) again to see it, or listen in the next step.

routes.source_title: Find the channel default
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1, trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13, over steps 1 to 16 at Rate /1 and 90 BPM. Its channel masks are Note C3 (60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, and the NOTE MASKS page is open; no step has a mask yet. Playback is stopped.

routes.source_title: Make the ending softer
routes.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen to two passes, then tap Play to stop. The screen is back on the channel defaults, the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows C, C, C, D: steps 1, 5 and 9 sound note 60 and step 13 sounds note 62, all at velocity 80, one beat apart.

routes.source_title: Return to the default view
routes.caption: While you hold (13,4), turn E3 right two detents. NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3: a pitch for step 13 only, two semitones above the default.

routes.source_title: Make the pickup quiet
routes.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X (the pattern notes decide pitch), Vel 80 and Len 1/2: the channel defaults the new trig will use until you give step 15 its own velocity.

routes.source_title: Open Masks
routes.caption: Choose pattern 1, tap (15,4) on Pattern Trig to add a trig on step 15, press Pattern (5,8) once to open the note view and tap (15,7) for degree 0. PATTERN NOTE PAT01 CH01 shows the tooltip Step 15 note set to 0 and a trig stripe on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15.

routes.source_title: Add a late trig
routes.caption: The project at the end of chapter 7: channel 1 plays degrees 0, 0, 0, 1 from pattern 1 with step 13 at velocity 50, channel 2 plays its bass, and C major is applied. Step 15 has no trig. Playback is stopped.

routes.source_title: Open channel 2's Device page
routes.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) again to open the note view, then tap (1,7) for degree 0 on step 1 and (9,3) for degree 4 on step 9. PATTERN NOTE PAT02 shows the tooltip Step 9 note set to 4. Only those two note taps are yours: the bright band along row 7 is the note view's degree 0 baseline, and the extra pad at (13,6) is not one of your notes and does not play. It is the note view also showing what channel 1 last played on step 13, D3 (degree 1); pattern 2 has no trig there.

routes.source_title: Write a root-and-fifth bass pattern
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays C, C, C, D over 16 steps at 90 BPM: step 13 has Note D3 (62) and Vel 50, the other trigs use C3 at 80. Channel 2, pattern 2 and a second MIDI output are still to be set up.

routes.source_title: Route channel 2 to its own output
routes.caption: Open the Device page for channel 2. The visible value is None; the channel and port selectors appear after a device is chosen.

routes.source_title: Finish the bass and hear both parts
routes.caption: Tap (9,8) for octave -1. The screen reads NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and the tooltip shows Ch. 2 octave: -1; (2,2) and (9,8) are lit.

routes.source_title: Optional: return to the two-part phrase
routes.caption: Tap (14,8) once more: Strategy reads ALL and all four trigs on row 4 light again. Play two passes and stop. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 60, 60, 60, 62 (velocity 80, 80, 80, 50): channel 1's Note and Vel masks supply the pitch and velocity, whichever pattern's trig fires.

routes.source_title: Optional: bring back every beat
routes.caption: Tap (14,8) once. MERGE MODES shows Strategy ONLY with the tooltip ONLY APPLIED, and the (14,8) button changes brightness. The button steps through Skip, Only, All and further strategies. Only plays a step only when more than one assigned pattern has a trig there: on row 4 just steps 1 and 9 stay bright.

routes.source_title: Optional: select overlapping beats
routes.caption: Optional detour. Select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot (2,2) to add pattern 2 next to pattern 1: MERGE MODES shows Patterns 01 02 and Strategy SKIP, the default. Play two passes and stop. Skip plays a step only when exactly one assigned pattern has a trig there, so with both patterns trigging steps 1 and 9, only steps 5 and 13 stay bright on row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding only 60 and 62 at velocity 50; the bass (48, 55) is unchanged.

routes.source_title: Optional: hear only the non-overlapping beats
routes.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two passes run, then tap Play to stop. While it plays the screen stays on NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and the Play pad (1,8) is lit. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 on port 1: notes 60, 60, 60 at velocity 80 and 62 at velocity 50, a beat apart. Channel 2 is on port 2: note 48 on step 1 and note 55 on step 9, both at velocity 100. That is the phrase above a low C and G.

routes.source_title: Choose the output and apply it
routes.caption: Turn E2 down the list to Device, the eighth task (seven detents below Masks), and press K3. The title row reads DEVICE with CH01. Only the Device row is listed, set to None: the MIDI channel and MIDI port rows appear once you choose a device.

routes.source_title: Open the Device page
routes.caption: A new, empty project with the transport stopped and nothing assigned to a channel. The pattern editor from chapter 1 is on screen. Channel 1 has no output chosen yet and no tempo has been set; the rest of the course uses MIDI port 1, MIDI channel 1 for channel 1.

routes.source_title: Set the tempo to 90 BPM
routes.caption: Press K3 to apply the draft. Notes from channel 1 now leave on MIDI port 1, MIDI channel 1. With your own gear, choose its device entry and set its port and channel; with no external gear, choose Polyperc 1 for the norns voice.

routes.source_title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2
routes.caption: Slot 1 holds the whole project, including the pickup on step 15 at velocity 35. Global length is the default 64, Repeats is 1 and Song mode is On; slots 2 and 3 are empty. Playback is stopped.

routes.source_title: Set slot 1 to one 16-step bar
routes.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 2 at (2,1) and tap Channel (3,8). The title reads CH01 S02 with no MUTE: channel 1 is audible in slot 2, so slot 2 keeps the full phrase.

routes.source_title: Set slot 2 to one 16-step bar
routes.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 1 at (1,1), tap (3,7) on the length fader, then tap (8,7) three times. The fader is row 7, columns 1 to 8: (3,7) jumps to 13 steps and each tap of (8,7) adds one, so 13 + 3 = 16. SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 01 shows Global length 16; Song mode reads AUTO there, which means Song mode is on and advancing.

routes.source_title: Check that the second section advances
routes.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 2 at (2,1), tap (3,7), then tap (8,7) three times: 13 + 3 = 16 again. SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 02 shows Global length 16.

routes.source_title: Check that slot 2 stays full
routes.caption: Select slot 1 at (1,1), tap Channel (3,8), then hold K1, tap (1,1) and release K1. K1 is the shift key from chapter 1: K1 plus a channel button mutes that channel in this slot only. The title reads CH01 MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 muted: slot 1 will play the bass alone.

routes.source_title: Mute channel 1 in slot 1
routes.caption: Tap Song (6,8), hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1), release slot 1 and tap (2,1) again to select slot 2. Holding slot 1 while you tap slot 2 copies the whole section (patterns, channel settings, masks and mutes). The screen reads SLOT SETUP, SONG 02, the tooltip says Song sequence 2 selected, and (2,1) is the bright slot button. The next two steps check the copy: slot 2 stays audible when slot 1 is muted.

routes.source_title: Hear the arrangement
routes.caption: Optional check. In Slot setup select Song mode, turn E3 right to On and press K3. SLOT SETUP, SONG 02 shows Song mode On, the default: the song moves from slot 1 to slot 2 and wraps to slot 1 because slot 3 is empty.

routes.source_title: Add a scale third to each step
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and no masks are set. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Chd1. The four chord rows Chd1-Chd4 add voices above each step's root, and X means no voice.

routes.source_title: Give each arpeggio note a short gate
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Arpeggio to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.

routes.source_title: Strum chord notes forward
routes.caption: From the half-step Strum slot, turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.

routes.source_title: Clear note-mask exceptions
routes.visible_owner_title: Adding Melodic Notes over Harmony and Drums
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

routes.source_title: Copy notes and dynamics across the four step pages
routes.caption: Press the page buttons (10,8), (11,8) and (12,8) in turn: the same four cells are lit on every page.

routes.source_title: Shape notes across the grid range
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Note the range buttons on row 8 are range-up (14,8), centre (15,8) and range-down (16,8). A press moves the window one degree up or down, a long press jumps to the top or bottom, and the centre button returns to the root page. Pattern Velocity has only two range buttons, (15,8) toward the top page and (16,8) toward the lower page, as the next lesson shows.

routes.source_title: Shape notes across the grid range
routes.caption: Hold range-down (16,8) for about a second: the window jumps to its lowest position. Tap (4,7), the bottom row: step 4 plays MIDI 48. Tap range-down again: the window cannot go lower, so (4,7) still plays MIDI 48.

routes.source_title: Hear Skip with overlapping patterns
routes.caption: Tap Channel (3,8) and tap pattern slot (2,2). Pattern 2 now plays on channel 1 beside pattern 1, and both slot buttons are lit.

routes.source_title: Add a trig mask to step 5
routes.caption: Release Step 5. Its E3 note is stored, but the step still has no trig, so the loop keeps playing the four C3 notes.

routes.source_title: Store a note before its trig
routes.caption: Turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until it reads 1/2. The four notes now have a half-step gate. A trig mask has no pattern note of its own, so a trig you add next will use these three channel defaults.

routes.source_title: Choose a trig algorithm
routes.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8). The preview closes and nothing was painted.

routes.source_title: Move a rhythm before committing
routes.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the fourth algorithm button (15,2) for Numeric. The Trig Algorithm screen marks Numeric as SELECTED. Numeric gives a sparse pattern, which makes shifts easy to see. The controls you will use on grid row 8 are Prime (16,8), Move left (10,8), Reset (11,8), Move right (12,8) and Cancel (14,8).

routes.source_title: Hear the copied phrase at velocity 117
routes.caption: Press the page buttons (10,8), (11,8) and (12,8) in turn: the same four cells are lit on every page.

routes.source_title: Give Step 4 a full-velocity accent
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Velocity the range buttons on row 8 differ from Pattern Note, which has three: here there are two, range-up at (15,8), toward the 127-68 page, and range-down at (16,8), toward the 58-0 page.

routes.source_title: Set step 4 to velocity 68
routes.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) three times to open Pattern Velocity. Each row of a step's column is a velocity level, 127 at the top. Tap (4,1). Press Play at (1,8), then Stop: step 4 plays at velocity 127 while steps 1-3 keep 127, 117, 107.

routes.source_title: Set step 4 to velocity 9
routes.caption: Tap down the column of step 4 to (4,4), playing after each tap: (4,2) is 48, (4,3) 39 and (4,4) 29. At (4,4) step 4 plays at velocity 29.

routes.source_title: Set the global song length
routes.caption: Tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once to add one. Global length reads 2. Press Play (1,8): the song plays only its first two steps and starts again, so the MIDI sent in this step is C and D (60, 62) over and over, never E or F. Press Play again to stop.

routes.source_title: Set the global song length
routes.caption: Tap the fader's right end (8,7), which adds one step. Global length reads 64 again, so the whole phrase plays.

routes.source_title: Capture a live keyboard phrase
routes.caption: Tap K1, open the CLOCK group and turn E3 back so Source reads internal. Following the external clock left the tempo at 100 BPM, so turn E2 to the tempo row and turn E3 until it reads 90 BPM; any tempo works, the notes' spacing simply follows it.

routes.source_title: Read Song slot lights
routes.caption: Turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Slot setup and press K3. Turn E3 up to Repeats 2 and press K3 to apply. Song mode is Off, so Repeats does not hold the slot for extra passes here; it only shows as the pass count on Song Playback.

routes.source_title: Set channel 2 to half speed
routes.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Clock page stays open and now reads CH02, with its own Rate /1.

routes.source_title: Return to the parent page
routes.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll to Clock and press K3. The Clock page for CH03 is showing.

routes.source_title: Set a channel fixed note
routes.caption: With no step held, turn E3 to 60 (C3). Slot 1 reads C5, this slot's name for MIDI note 60 (it numbers octaves two higher than the C3 used elsewhere in this manual). This is the channel's default pitch, the note every step plays unless it has its own lock.

routes.source_title: Play a valid step range
routes.caption: Channel 1 sends to the example MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. The channel range is steps 1 to 4, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.

routes.source_title: Hear positive chord acceleration
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Each gap is now 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 step. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Accel Mod.

routes.source_title: Hear negative chord acceleration
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Each gap is now 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 step. Acceleration works on Spread, so with Spread at zero it would do nothing. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Accel Mod.

routes.source_title: Play a gated arpeggio
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Arpeggio to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.

routes.source_title: Play the chord in forward order
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Pattern and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to -> (forward). Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Mute Chord Root.

routes.source_title: Set a constant chord spread
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2: the notes will be half a step apart. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Spread.

routes.source_title: Play a forward strum
routes.caption: From the half-step Strum slot, turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.

routes.source_title: Raise chord voice velocities
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Velocity Mod. Chord Note Strum (1/2), Chord Pattern (-> forward) and Mute Chord Root (X, off) are already assigned, so the root and four chord notes strum half a step apart.

routes.source_title: Open the channel clock
routes.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). The header returns to CH01 and Device shows CC Device again: each channel keeps its own device.

routes.source_title: Set channel swing to 25 while Interlock runs
routes.caption: Two 8-step channels at 90 BPM. Channel 1 has Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and Pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has one anchor trig on step 5 and is channel 1's Interlock leader. Interlock removes channel 1's addition on step 5, so channel 1's grid shows steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 lit. Clock Rate is /1 and Swing is not set (X).

routes.source_title: Find the Swing type row without changing feel
routes.caption: Turn E2 left until Rate is selected, the first row (it reads /1, the default). The list shows Rate, Feel source and Swing type together, so you can read the channel's clock and feel settings at a glance.

routes.source_title: Set smooth shuffle amount to 50
routes.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale, with Rate /1. Its Clock page is set to Shuffle with Feel Smooth, Basis 9 and Amount 1. Timing is counted in pulses: each step is 24 pulses, so at Amount 1 the notes sit almost exactly on the straight grid, at 0, 24, 48 and 72. First compare Amount 0, 50 and 100 with Smooth Feel and Basis 9 unchanged. The last three checkpoints are an optional stronger-groove extension using Basis 6.

routes.source_title: Slide a CC between locks
routes.caption: With no step held, press K3. Slot 1 reads 63 again and gains an S in its corner, so every lock of CC 1 slides toward the next one.

routes.source_title: Leave a device parameter off
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped. Channel 1's output is a example MIDI device whose parameter Control 1 sends MIDI CC 1 from 0 to 127 and has an Off position shown as X. No value is stored for Control 1 yet. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

routes.source_title: Lock a CC to one step
routes.caption: Press K3 to confirm the assignment and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 right 36 detents from 63 to 99. Slot 1 shows 99 with an L in its corner while the step is held. The stored value, 63, is not changed. Release the step.

routes.source_title: Slide one step’s CC
routes.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and press K3. Slot 1 shows 24 with an S in its corner while step 1 is held, so only the slide that starts at step 1 is on. Release the step.

routes.source_title: Open the channel clock
routes.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). The header returns to CH01 and Device shows CC Device again: each channel keeps its own device.

routes.source_title: Keep anchors and accent the additions
routes.caption: Turn E2 to Add amount, which reads 100: every candidate addition is admitted. Turn E2 two detents on to Add accent, which reads 70 and scales the velocity of the added trigs to 70 percent. Both settings are already at these values; you only read them here. The grid shows the anchors on steps 1 to 4 and the additions on steps 5 and 7.

routes.source_title: Place two voices smoothly
routes.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony; the header reads VOICE LEADING CH01.

routes.source_title: Shape notes across the grid range
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Note the range buttons on row 8 are range-up (14,8), centre (15,8) and range-down (16,8). A press moves the window one degree up or down, a long press jumps to the top or bottom, and the centre button returns to the root page. Pattern Velocity has only two range buttons, (15,8) toward the top page and (16,8) toward the lower page, as the next lesson shows.

routes.source_title: Shape accents and rests
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Velocity the range buttons on row 8 differ from Pattern Note, which has three: here there are two, range-up at (15,8), toward the 127-68 page, and range-down at (16,8), toward the 58-0 page.

routes.source_title: Elektron Program Changes: Default Off (canonical walkthrough linked)
routes.caption: In the Song editor (grid (6,8)) set Global length to 4 steps, copy slot 1 into slot 2 (hold slot 1, press slot 2) and, with slot 2 selected, raise the channel octave by one (11,8) so slot 2 sounds an octave above slot 1. Return to the Song editor and select slot 1 (1,1): slot 1 is bright and slot 2 is lit.

context_handoff.label: Open the Elektron Program Changes Off lesson
context_handoff.reason: The same retained scene supports both settings. Its canonical Off walkthrough explains the Digitakt baseline Programs and distinguishes them from slot-change announcements.

routes.source_title: Match the receiver’s program-change channel
routes.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Elektron p.change channel and turn E3 left nine detents from the default 10 to 1. The row shows 1.

routes.source_title: Choose the clock source
routes.caption: Turn E2 to the tempo row. It reads 100 BPM: while Source was midi the incoming clock set the tempo, and switching Source back does not restore your own. Turn E3 ten detents down to bring it back to 90 BPM, the tempo the project used before.

routes.source_title: Set a fixed C3 phrase
routes.caption: With no step held, turn E3 to 60 (C3). Slot 1 reads C5, this slot's name for MIDI note 60 (it numbers octaves two higher than the C3 used elsewhere in this manual). This is the channel's default pitch, the note every step plays unless it has its own lock.

routes.source_title: Fragments: Compare the five merge strategies
routes.caption: Under Foundation, Note, Velocity and Length modes still edit. Select each on Merge modes and turn E3 right to read UP, then left to read AVERAGE again.

routes.source_title: Let each fragment keep its source notes
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays through the example MIDI device on an 8-step loop at 90 BPM, rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6. Both patterns are assigned to channel 1 and Strategy is still SKIP. Merge modes is open for channel 1. In this scene a Seed makes a repeatable draw of which pattern each fragment comes from: the same seed always gives the same choice.

routes.source_title: Enable channel mask quantisation
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. On enables full scale mapping; Off disables it. An absent step lock uses the channel, and channel X uses the global option. An explicitly stored step X skips the channel and uses the global option directly; clearing it with K2 restores channel inheritance. In the state lists, X without a stored step lock means no exception; explicit step X is named separately. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / Off / On. The global Off is inherited by the channel, step 1 is Off and step 2 is On, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

routes.source_title: Set one step’s mask quantisation Off
routes.caption: State: On / X / X / On. With no step held, turn the channel value down to X (unset). The global On applies again: 62, 65, 71, 60. Step 2 keeps its own On lock.

routes.source_title: Quantise note masks to the scale
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1; both are already set in the scale editor. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Snap note masks to scale is On, while Quantise note masks (the global full-quantisation option) and Lock merged to pent. are Off. With Snap alone the masks play as written, 60, 64, 69, 71 in the MIDI strip, because Degree and Rotation affect masks only under full quantisation. On enables full scale mapping; Off disables it. An absent step lock uses the channel, and channel X uses the global option. An explicitly stored step X skips the channel and uses the global option directly; clearing it with K2 restores channel inheritance. In the state lists, X without a stored step lock means no exception; explicit step X is named separately. Each step below lists the state as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / X / X.

routes.source_title: Each channel keeps its own device and rate
routes.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). The header returns to CH01 and Device shows CC Device again: each channel keeps its own device.

routes.source_title: Save D major, then apply it
routes.caption: Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3 to save. Slot 2 now holds D major, but it is still not applied.

routes.source_title: Set the global song length
routes.caption: Tap the fader's right end (8,7), which adds one step. Global length reads 64 again, so the whole phrase plays.

routes.source_title: Reopen the trig algorithm list
routes.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8). The preview closes and nothing was painted.

routes.source_title: Inspect a step and return
routes.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll to Clock and press K3. The Clock page for CH03 is showing.

routes.source_title: Save D major, then apply it
routes.caption: Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3 to save. Slot 2 now holds D major, but it is still not applied.

routes.source_title: Set the global song length
routes.caption: Tap the fader's right end (8,7), which adds one step. Global length reads 64 again, so the whole phrase plays.

routes.source_title: Enable the Ensemble group on channel 4
routes.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 4. Then turn E2 to Ensemble and press K3. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH04.

routes.source_title: Set the lower register bound to MIDI 50
routes.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony. Its list holds Mode, Register, Tone Map, Result and the Entry / Failure row used later. Turn E3 to set Mode to PATTERN, select Register with E2 and press K3.

routes.source_title: Harmony: Place two voices smoothly
routes.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony; the header reads VOICE LEADING CH01.

routes.source_title: Related context: choose natural minor before keyboard mapping
routes.caption: Close the menu and play the white keys from C3 up to C4 on the keyboard. In C major they sound as written: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71, 72. The MIDI strip lists the notes Mosaic sent.

context_handoff.label: Open the natural-minor Scale-field step in MIDI Controller Options
context_handoff.reason: This route shows the Scale-field selection checkpoint. Use the complete scene link above for the resulting keyboard notes and degree-II mapping.

routes.source_title: Related context: rotate the keyboard voicing
routes.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale rotations and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

context_handoff.label: Open the complete keyboard-rotation lesson in MIDI Controller Options
context_handoff.reason: This canonical lesson includes the rotation action and captured keyboard output; the scene link above opens the full multi-step setup and comparison.

routes.source_title: Honour Scale Transpose: compare the recorded C3–C4 phrase
routes.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale transpose and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

routes.source_title: Chain song slots an octave apart
routes.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). The octave button lights and the footer reads Ch. 1 octave: 1: channel 1 will play one octave higher in this slot.

routes.source_title: Copy a slot, then change the copy
routes.caption: A fresh session with Song mode On, its default. Channel 1 plays its default phrase through the example MIDI device and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1; nothing is playing. The song has one slot, Song 01.

routes.source_title: Leave room around a leader’s anchors
routes.caption: Select Interlock with E2 and press K3 to open the Interlock page for channel 1. This keeps channel 1's additions out of the way of another channel's anchors.

routes.source_title: Average merged note lengths
routes.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are both assigned to channel 1, with the same trigs on the same steps: pattern 1's notes are 2 steps long and pattern 2's are 4 steps long. Length merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8). Length merge is set with K1 (shift) held, which turns the velocity merge button (16,8) into the length button.

routes.source_title: Route a macro and remove its depth
routes.caption: The norns matrix and toolkit mods are installed and enabled. Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a CC device with Rate /1, the sequencer is stopped, and the Matrix has no routes yet. The Device page for CH01 is showing.

routes.source_title: Advanced: Set up a clocked LFO at full depth
routes.caption: Tap K1 and open MODS > MATRIX. Choose MOSAIC CH 1: CC DEVICE and select Fixed Note, the parameter the LFO will drive. Press K3 to open Fixed Note's sources and turn E2 to lfo 1; its row shows dashes, no depth yet. Hold E3 turning right until lfo 1's depth reads 1.00, so the LFO controls Fixed Note at full strength.

routes.source_title: Restrict every note to five degrees
routes.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8), hold step 1 (1,4) and tap step 7 (7,4). Steps 1 to 7 light up and step 8 stays dark, so the channel range is steps 1-7.

routes.source_title: Send lock values before their notes
routes.caption: On Trig params, hold each of steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 in turn and turn E3 to give it its own CC 1 lock value. Then tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, choose MOSAIC and select Lock lead time (ms) in the Parameter locks section. Turn E3 to 0. At 0 each lock value is sent at the same moment as its step, together with the note. This is the original timing.

routes.source_title: Lock merged notes to pentatonic: Off
routes.caption: Hold the velocity merge key (16,8), tap pattern slot 3 at (3,2) and release. Slots 1 and 2 stay lit as the assigned patterns and slot 3 stays dim because it is not assigned: it only supplies the velocity of the merged notes. Note merge stays on its default, Average.

routes.source_title: Lock merged notes to pentatonic: On
routes.caption: Hold the velocity merge key (16,8), tap pattern slot 3 at (3,2) and release. Slots 1 and 2 stay lit as the assigned patterns and slot 3 stays dim because it is not assigned: it only supplies the velocity of the merged notes. Note merge stays on its default, Average.

routes.source_title: Lock random notes to pentatonic: Off
routes.caption: Assign Twos Random Note to the second slot in the same way. It stays at 0, so it adds nothing to this lesson; only Random Note is used.

routes.source_title: Lock random notes to pentatonic: On
routes.caption: Assign Twos Random Note to the second slot in the same way. It stays at 0, so it adds nothing to this lesson; only Random Note is used.

routes.source_title: Lock transposition without losing the global setting
routes.caption: Keep holding step 1 and press (16,8) twelve more times. Each press adds one semitone, up to +12. The first note jumps an octave to MIDI 72. Steps 2 to 4 still follow the zero lock on step 2 and stay at MIDI 62, 64 and 65.

routes.source_title: Keep a stored value while locking a step
routes.caption: Press K3 to confirm the assignment and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 right 36 detents from 63 to 99. Slot 1 shows 99 with an L in its corner while the step is held. The stored value, 63, is not changed. Release the step.

routes.source_title: Context: Set and clear Note masks at both scopes
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

routes.source_title: Compare Step 2’s local octave with the channel octave
routes.caption: Release step 2, press Play (1,8), then Stop. The MIDI strip reads 36, 38, 40 and 41 (C1, D1, E1, F1). A lock equal to the channel octave changes nothing you can hear. A low channel octave suits a bass line.

routes.source_title: Move between parameter locks
routes.caption: With no step held, press K3. Slot 1 reads 63 again and gains an S in its corner, so every lock of CC 1 slides toward the next one.

routes.source_title: Assign Fixed Note and hear four steps
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Trig params screen is open on its parameter list, showing Fixed Note; every slot is empty (None).

routes.source_title: Play four steps against three
routes.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device and press K3. The header reads CH02: this second channel will play a three-step loop.

routes.source_title: Play sixteen steps against five
routes.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 at (5,4) and release step 1. The footer reads Channel 2 length changed: channel 2 loops steps 1 to 5, and its three figure steps are lit.

routes.source_title: Restart both loops at the section boundary
routes.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Reset on song seq change and turn E3 right to On (the default). The row reads On.

routes.source_title: Enable group 1 on channel 4
routes.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 4. Then turn E2 to Ensemble and press K3. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH04.

routes.source_title: Set a Note default and clear each scope
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

routes.source_title: Accent Step 1 and silence Step 2
routes.caption: With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 50. This channel velocity mask replaces the pattern's velocities: every note now plays at 50, so the whole phrase is softer. Pitch and timing are unchanged.

routes.source_title: Clear a note mask without clearing its neighbour
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. The Masks page (Channel tasks, then Masks) is open on Note. The channel's Note mask default is 67 (G3), step 1 has its own mask 72 and step 2 has 74, so the MIDI strip reads 72, 74, 67, 67.

routes.source_title: Context: Add a scale third with Chd1
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and no masks are set. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Chd1. The four chord rows Chd1-Chd4 add voices above each step's root, and X means no voice.

context_handoff.label: Open the scale-third chord lesson in Adding Chords
context_handoff.reason: This action adds the scale third above each root; the canonical walkthrough is in Adding Chords.

routes.source_title: Change the ending of a four-note melody
routes.caption: Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 right until it reads E4 (16 detents) and release. The melody ends on E4: 72, 74, 79, 76.

routes.source_title: Set a ghost note and an accent
routes.caption: Hold step 3 at (3,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads 100 and release. Step 3 is the accent: the MIDI strip shows 80, 80, 100, 80.

routes.source_title: Set the channel Note default to G3
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

routes.source_title: Accent one note and silence the next
routes.caption: With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 50. This channel velocity mask replaces the pattern's velocities: every note now plays at 50, so the whole phrase is softer. Pitch and timing are unchanged.

routes.source_title: Hear the result after Redo
routes.caption: Tap Play: 72, 62, 64, 65, so only the first edit is back. Then turn E3 right once more. The counter is back at 2 of 2.

routes.source_title: Hear the result after Undo
routes.caption: Tap Play: the phrase is 72, 76, 64, 65 at velocities 90, 80, 107, 97, because steps 1 and 2 carry your edits. Now, in History, turn E3 one detent left. The counter reads 1 of 2: the second edit is undone.

routes.source_title: Play the original phrase
routes.caption: Turn E2 down to History and press K3. The Memory screen shows your position in the channel's remembered edits, as 'position of total'. It reads 0 of 0 because nothing has been edited yet.

routes.source_title: Average merged note lengths
routes.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are both assigned to channel 1, with the same trigs on the same steps: pattern 1's notes are 2 steps long and pattern 2's are 4 steps long. Length merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8). Length merge is set with K1 (shift) held, which turns the velocity merge button (16,8) into the length button.

routes.source_title: Hear Skip on overlapping trigs
routes.caption: Press K2, turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Merge modes and press K3 to return to the Merge modes screen, then turn E2 down to Strategy, the trig merge. It reads SKIP, the default: a step plays only if exactly one pattern has a trig there. Steps 1 and 2 are in both patterns and drop out; only steps 3 and 4 remain.

routes.source_title: Average merged note pitches
routes.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are assigned to channel 1, so channel 1 merges them. Pattern 1 plays scale degrees 1, 3, 5, 7 (C E G B) and pattern 2 plays degrees 3, 5, 7, 1 (E G B C). Note merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (15,8). Pentatonic snapping of merged notes is off: before you try this, tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Lock merged to pent. to Off. Left On (the default), merged notes snap to the five-note pentatonic version of the scale and you hear different pitches.

routes.source_title: Hear a Foundation phrase
routes.caption: Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads FOUNDATION (grid key (14,8) steps through the same choices). Select Active: it reads FOUNDATION. The first pattern stays whole and the second only adds notes.

routes.source_title: Average merged velocities
routes.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned with different velocities for four notes: 127, 117, 107, 97 and 100, 100, 100, 100. Its notes come from a third pattern, shown on the screen as Note mode PAT 4 (pattern 4 is not assigned to the channel; all its notes are MIDI 67), so only velocity changes. Velocity merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8).

routes.source_title: Build over two channel loops
routes.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps on the example MIDI device with Merge Shape set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, on steps 1 to 4) is the protected Anchor and pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) offers additions; both are assigned. Add amount is 100 and Add accent 70, so all candidate additions are allowed and sound at 70 percent of their velocity. The Phrase settings are still at their defaults, the norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

routes.source_title: Foundation and All: who decides the trigs
routes.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the example MIDI device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Both patterns are assigned, Add amount is 100 and Add accent is 70. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

routes.source_title: Merge Shape: Keep anchors and accent the additions
routes.caption: Turn E2 to Add amount, which reads 100: every candidate addition is admitted. Turn E2 two detents on to Add accent, which reads 70 and scales the velocity of the added trigs to 70 percent. Both settings are already at these values; you only read them here. The grid shows the anchors on steps 1 to 4 and the additions on steps 5 and 7.

routes.source_title: Skip and All on a step both patterns trig
routes.caption: Turn E3 left to SKIP. The footer reads SKIP APPLIED and the Strategy key (14,8) dims. Skip applies a trig only if it appears in exactly one selected pattern, so step 3, where both patterns trig, will not sound.

routes.source_title: Merge Shape: Compare the five merge strategies
routes.caption: Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads FOUNDATION (grid key (14,8) steps through the same choices). Select Active: it reads FOUNDATION. The first pattern stays whole and the second only adds notes.

routes.source_title: Teach a relative MIDI controller
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped. A MIDI controller on input port 1, channel 1 is connected and sends relative CC 20: a value of 63 means one step down and 65 one step up. Nothing is mapped yet and the velocity mask is Off (X).

routes.source_title: MIDI Controller Options: Select natural minor
routes.caption: Close the menu and play the white keys from C3 up to C4 on the keyboard. In C major they sound as written: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71, 72. The MIDI strip lists the notes Mosaic sent.

routes.source_title: MIDI Controller Options: Rotate the keyboard voicing
routes.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale rotations and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

routes.source_title: Panic by holding Channel while on Song
routes.caption: Press Song (6,8). The Song page opens (Song Playback, SONG 01) and Song is the lit page button. Panic only works from the button of a page you are not on, so every other page button, including Channel (3,8), is a panic button from here.

routes.source_title: Panic by holding Pattern while on Song
routes.caption: Press Song (6,8). The Song page opens (Song Playback, SONG 01) and Song is the lit page button. Panic only works from the button of a page you are not on, so every other page button, including Pattern (5,8), is a panic button from here.

routes.source_title: Apply Polyperc 1
routes.caption: Turn E3 until the Device row reads Polyperc 1. The footer says “Press K3 to confirm”, so this is still a draft.

routes.source_title: Musical Merge and Voice Leading: Keep anchors and accent the additions
routes.caption: Turn E2 to Add amount, which reads 100: every candidate addition is admitted. Turn E2 two detents on to Add accent, which reads 70 and scales the velocity of the added trigs to 70 percent. Both settings are already at these values; you only read them here. The grid shows the anchors on steps 1 to 4 and the additions on steps 5 and 7.

routes.source_title: Musical Merge and Voice Leading: Place two voices smoothly
routes.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony; the header reads VOICE LEADING CH01.

routes.source_title: Musical Merge and Voice Leading: Compare the five merge strategies
routes.caption: Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads FOUNDATION (grid key (14,8) steps through the same choices). Select Active: it reads FOUNDATION. The first pattern stays whole and the second only adds notes.

routes.source_title: Mute the chord root
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Mute Chord Root and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to On. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Velocity Mod.

routes.source_title: Hear the unmuted channel
routes.caption: Tap Play to stop. Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens again, so channel 1 is unmuted.

routes.source_title: Move between parameter locks
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign CC 1 and K2 to return. Slot 1 now reads 63, the stored value, with no marker in its corner, because no step has a lock for it yet.

routes.source_title: Slide only one source lock
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign CC 1 and K2 to return. Slot 1 now reads 63, the stored value, with no marker in its corner, because no step has a lock for it yet.

routes.source_title: Enter a project name and keep the arrangement
routes.caption: Press K2 in name entry. The Save project menu returns and neither named project file is created.

routes.source_title: Set channel probability to 100
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Fixed Note to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 to 65 (F3): every note is now F3. Turn E2 to the next slot and open the Trig Probability picker.

routes.source_title: Set channel probability to 0
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Trig Probability and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 100. Tap Play (1,8) and tap it again to stop: the MIDI strip lists all four steps at pitch 65 with velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. Then turn E3 up a few more detents; the value stays at 100. Play and stop again: every trig still sounds.

routes.source_title: Override one step’s probability
routes.caption: Press K3 to assign Trig Probability and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 100. Tap Play (1,8) and tap it again to stop: the MIDI strip lists all four steps at pitch 65 with velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. Then turn E3 up a few more detents; the value stays at 100. Play and stop again: every trig still sounds.

routes.source_title: Add a scale-third chord voice and override it on one step
routes.expected_visible_text:
1. On Masks, set Chd1 to 3rd; play the phrase to hear each root with its scale third.
2. Hold step 1 and set Chd1 to 5th; release it and compare that step with the channel default.
3. Clear step 1 with K2 so it inherits 3rd again.
Outcome: Chord mask values are scale intervals. The step-specific fifth overrides the channel third only on step 1; clearing restores the third.

routes.source_title: Make one step override a channel Note default, then restore inheritance
routes.visible_owner_title: Adding Melodic Notes over Harmony and Drums
routes.expected_visible_text:
1. On Masks, set the channel Note default to G3.
2. Hold step 1 and set its Note to C4; release the step and check that the channel readout returns to G3 while step 1 keeps its exception.
3. Add a D4 exception on step 2, then clear step 1 and finally clear all step exceptions with K1+K2.
Outcome: A held-step Note value overrides the channel default for that step. Clearing exceptions restores the channel Note to G3 across the pattern.

routes.source_title: Add a melodic note to an empty step, then toggle only its trig
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: the channel range is steps 1–8; steps 1–4 have trigs and step 5 at (5,4) has none.

1. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Select Note with E2 and turn E3 to C3. Select Vel with E2 and turn E3 to 80; select Len with E2 and turn E3 to 1/2.
2. Return to Note with E2. Hold step 5 at (5,4), turn E3 clockwise until Note reads E3 (MIDI 64), then release. Its note is stored but the step remains silent.
3. Hold K1, tap step 5 at (5,4), then release K1. The trig mask adds E3 at the channel velocity and length. Hold K1 and tap the same step again, then release K1, to remove that trig mask. The Note exception remains.

Outcome: the note mask supplies a pitch; the separate trig gesture decides whether the empty step sounds.

routes.source_title: Preview a shifted Numeric pattern, cancel it, then commit a fresh preview
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: use a new empty project with playback stopped and Record Off. Select Pattern 1 on channel 1. The [Move a rhythm before committing](#adding-trigs/paint-shift-and-cancel) capture starts with 8 flashing trigs at Shift 0 (steps 5, 13, 21, 29 and onward). Its controls are Prime (16,8), Move right (12,8) and Cancel (14,8). The captured result is replayed by the manual; on hardware, the preview uses the selected Numeric settings.

1. Select Numeric Repetitor at (15,2) and press Prime (16,8). Check the Preview readout: Algorithm Numeric, Shift 0 and 8 trigs.

2. Tap Move right (12,8) once. The flashing steps shift one step to the right, starting at step 6; the readout is Shift +1.

3. Tap Cancel (14,8). Check Preview OFF and Trigs NONE; the pattern has not been painted.

4. Press Prime (16,8) again, tap Move right (12,8) once and press Prime again to commit. The new pattern stays one step to the right; only this committed preview is painted.

Outcome: Cancel discards the preview without writing trigs. A fresh shifted preview can be committed; the captured result shows the preview state, while the project changes only after the final Prime.

routes.source_title: Shorten and restore a phrase
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays a four-step motif on steps 1 to 4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Its channel range is steps 1 to 4 and the global length is 64 steps. Playback is stopped.
1. Press Song (6,8). The length fader is on row 7, columns 1 to 8.
2. Tap (2,7) to set the global length to one step (the buttons between the ends jump to 1, 13, 32, 38, 51 and 64), then tap (8,7) once to add one step. Song Playback shows Global length reading two.
3. Press Play (1,8). Only the first two steps play: MIDI 60, 62, 60, 62 and so on. The channel range is still steps 1 to 4, so nothing is deleted.
4. Press Stop (1,8). Tap (8,7) twice to set the global length to four steps, then press Play. All four steps return: 60, 62, 64, 65.
Use this to loop a short fragment of a longer motif without editing it, then restore the full phrase. The end buttons (1,7) and (8,7) change the length one step at a time. The captured example Set the global song length, below, uses the two end buttons on the Song Playback screen: it takes one step off 64 (63) and puts it back. Its later Play result auditions the chosen length; inspect that result to compare the shortened phrase. Stop before restoring the full length.

routes.source_title: Return from a held-step edit to the page you were using
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: playback is stopped, channel 3 is selected and its Masks page is open. No step is held and Note reads X. This example separates a step-only edit from inspecting a step while another Channel task is open.

1. Hold step 5 at grid (5,4). The header reads NOTE MASKS CH03 ST05. Turn E2 anticlockwise until Note is selected, then turn E3 clockwise one detent. The step Note changes from X to C-2 (MIDI 0), the lowest note value. A Note mask alone does not create a trig.
2. Release step 5. The header returns to NOTE MASKS CH03 and the channel Note still reads X: the C-2 exception belongs only to step 5.
3. Turn E1 until Channel tasks opens. Turn E2 to Clock and press K3. Check the Clock page for CH03.
4. Hold step 9 at grid (9,4). The screen temporarily shows NOTE MASKS CH03 ST09. Do not hold step 5 or change a value during this separate inspection.
5. Release step 9. Clock returns, because it was the page you were using before the hold.

Use a step hold to inspect or edit one exception without losing your place in another Channel task. The earlier step-5 edit and the later step-9 inspection are separate gestures.

routes.source_title: Build the recording: Straight, then swung
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: Use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and global Swing 0, with playback stopped. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and Polyperc 1 to channel 2. Set both channel ranges to 1-16 and turn Snap note masks to scale Off.

Controls used here: open Channel at (3,8), select the channel on row 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 and K3 to open Device, Masks or Clock. On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 selects a value and K3 applies it. In Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel or Len and E3 changes the value; hold K1 and tap a step to add a trig, or hold a step and turn E3 for a local value. Open Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are on row 1. Hold slot 1 and tap slot 2 to copy. Set tempo through Song tasks → Tempo & feel. Each channel has its own Clock page; E2 selects Swing type or amount, E3 changes it and K3 applies it.

1. On channel 1 Masks, set Note MIDI 36, Vel 80 and Len half a step.

2. Add trigs at steps 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10, 13 and 14.

3. Set steps 2, 6, 10 and 14 to MIDI 37; set steps 5 and 13 to MIDI 38. Steps 1 and 9 stay at MIDI 36.

4. On channel 2 Masks, set Note MIDI 48, Vel 60 and Len half a step.

5. Add trigs at steps 1, 4, 9 and 12.

6. Set steps 4 and 12 to MIDI 55 and step 9 to MIDI 52.

7. In Song Editor, set slot 1 length to 32 steps.

8. Copy slot 1 to slot 2; leave slot 2 at length 32.

9. With slot 2 selected, open Clock for channel 1. Select Swing type with E2, choose Swing with E3 and press K3.

10. On channel 1 Clock, select Swing with E2, set it to 25 with E3 and press K3.

11. Repeat steps 9–10 on channel 2. Leave slot 1 straight.

12. Play the two slots in order. Bars 1–2 are straight; bars 3–4 use Swing 25, moving only the second step in each pair. Stop and select slot 1 to restore the straight version.

Listen for: Bars 1-2 are straight. Bars 3-4 use Swing 25; only the second step in each pair moves.

Restore: Select slot 1 to hear the straight version again, then stop playback and return to the original project.

routes.source_title: Shape a CC ramp between two step locks
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: channel 1 is routed to the example MIDI device and its active phrase has steps 1–4.

1. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, set the device’s Control 1 to 63, then return to Mosaic. Open Channel tasks with E1, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3.
2. Select slot 1 with E2, press K2 to open its assignment list, turn E3 to CC 1, press K3 to assign it, then press K2 to return. The slot reads the stored 63.
3. Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 anticlockwise to 24 and release. Hold step 3 at (3,4), turn E3 clockwise to 96 and release. Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 anticlockwise to 48 and release.
4. Hold step 1 again and press K3, then release. The slide belongs to that step. Pressing K3 with no step held would instead toggle the channel-wide slide.
5. Tap Play at (1,8), let two loops run, then stop. CC 1 glides from 24 toward 96, followed by the direct jump to 48 at step 4.
6. Reopen PARAMS > MOSAIC and inspect Control 1: the stored value remains 63.

Outcome: the local slide shapes the emitted controller values without overwriting the stored device value.

routes.source_title: Send program changes on channel 1
routes.expected_visible_text:
A MIDI Program Change asks a receiver to select a program, often a pattern. Use this when your receiver listens for program changes on a channel other than 10. Finish Follow Mosaic's slots with a Digitakt first, so Elektron program changes is On and the song has two slots.
1. Make sure the receiver listens for program changes on channel 1.
2. In PARAMS > MOSAIC select Elektron p.change channel and turn E3 left nine detents from 10 to 1.
3. While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1). Mosaic sends program change C0 01: the strip lists Program 1 (ch 1) instead of Program 1 (ch 10) (C9 01).

routes.source_title: Follow Mosaic's slots with a Digitakt
routes.expected_visible_text:
Purpose: A Program Change asks the receiver to select a pattern when Mosaic changes song slots. If no Digitakt is connected, check the listed MIDI bytes instead of expecting a sound change.

1. Give the song two slots. In the Song editor (grid (6,8)) hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it. Set Global length to 4 steps if you want to hear the changes quickly.
2. On channel 1's Device screen choose the Digitakt configuration. Set the receiver to accept program changes on MIDI channel 10, its default. If you have no Digitakt, watch the MIDI output instead: the strip lists Program 1 (ch 10) and Program 0 (ch 10), the bytes C9 01 and C9 00.
3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Elektron program changes and turn E3 to On.
4. While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1). Mosaic sends program change C9 01 and the receiver switches to its pattern 2 (wire value 1); the strip lists Program 1 (ch 10). Press slot 1 for pattern 1 (C9 00, Program 0 (ch 10)).
5. Select slot 1 and press Play. Each slot change is announced once, just before the new slot sounds.

routes.source_title: Set four-step fragments
routes.expected_visible_text:
Musical purpose: build one phrase from two patterns, taking the first half of the loop from one pattern and the second half from the other. Each half keeps its source notes and velocities.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop at 90 BPM and Rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97). Pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6, and both are assigned to the channel. Strategy is SKIP.

1. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, select Merge modes and press K3. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until it reads FRAGMENTS. Active reads FRAGMENTS. A strategy choice applies at once and needs no K3.
2. Turn E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape and press K3. Select Rhythm with E2 and press K3. The Fragments list opens: Size 8, Keep anchor OFF, Seed 0; edits on this list are drafts until you press K3.
3. Select Size and turn E3 once left. Size reads 4, so the loop is cut into two fragments: steps 1 to 4 and steps 5 to 8.
4. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the channel grid lights only step 3, because Seed 0 gives the first fragment to Pattern 2 and the second to Pattern 1, and Pattern 1 has no trigs in the second half.
5. Press Play (grid (1,8)), listen to two loops and press Stop. Each loop plays a single C (MIDI 60) at velocity 100, and Pattern 1’s E on step 3 is not mixed in.
6. Select Seed with E2 and turn E3 once right. Seed reads 1, and a seed always makes the same choice, so Seed 1 gives the first fragment to Pattern 1 and the second to Pattern 2.
7. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the grid lights steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6.
8. Press Play. Each loop plays C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and then Pattern 2’s C on step 6 at velocity 100, then press Stop.

Edits stay drafts until K3, so change Size and Seed first and apply once if you prefer. Turn Keep anchor ON to let the anchor pattern fill empty positions. Open Phrase and set Variation to Per phrase if you want new sources each phrase.

The seed is a repeatable dice roll: seed 0 and seed 1 above give opposite choices for the two halves, and every other seed gives its own choice that always repeats. Try a few more seeds and keep the one you like.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured Fragments seed and playback workflow](#fragments/fragments-seed-source-choice).

routes.source_title: Return from a held-step edit to the page you were using
routes.expected_visible_text:
Purpose: this recorded check distinguishes the temporary held-step Masks header from the Clock page that returns on release. It also shows that a local C-2 exception does not change channel Note X. See [Inspect a step and return](#grid-menu-navigation/hold-step-return) for the captured headers and local result.

Starting point: Playback is stopped, channel 3 is selected, and Channel tasks > Clock is open. No step is held; channel Note is X.

1. Hold step 9 at grid (9,4). The screen temporarily shows NOTE MASKS CH03 ST09. Release step 9. The Clock page returns.

2. Hold step 5 at grid (5,4). The screen shows NOTE MASKS CH03 ST05. Turn E2 anticlockwise until Note is selected, then turn E3 clockwise one detent. Step 5 changes from X to C-2 (MIDI 0). A Note mask alone does not create a trig.

3. Release step 5. The Clock page returns. Open Channel tasks > Masks and confirm channel 3 Note still reads X; the C-2 exception belongs only to step 5. Return to Clock if you want to leave the example as you found it.

Outcome: Holding and releasing step 9 while Clock is open temporarily shows Masks and restores Clock. The separate step-5 edit remains local to that step, while the channel Note default remains X.

routes.source_title: Map three relative values
routes.expected_visible_text:
Goal: map selected Pattern notes to fixed Harmony voices and registers, then inspect the planned and sent pitches in Result.

Musical purpose: pin chosen written notes to fixed voices of a chord frame, each limited to its own register, so a note that repeats in the phrase always lands on the same pitch. Choose Pattern when you want to decide which written note goes to which voice; choose Revoice when the chord notes are already written and you want Mosaic to arrange their octaves. In this phrase the notes are all different, so the repeat rule is explained at the end rather than heard.

Terms used below: a written value is the relative note of a step (0 to 3 here); a voice is Bass, Inner 1 to 3 or Top; a register is the range of MIDI notes a voice may use; RAW means the value is not mapped and keeps its own pitch.

Starting point: channel 1 plays one pattern, C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (written values 0, 1, 2, 3; MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), at 90 BPM. Harmony is Off.

1. Turn E1 for Channel tasks, select Harmony with E2 and press K3. The Voice leading list opens with Mode OFF.

2. Select Mode with E2 and turn E3 twice right (Off, Revoice, Pattern). Mode reads PATTERN and a Tone Map row appears. The change is a draft until K3.

3. Select Tone Map with E2 and press K3. The Tone Map lists one row for each written value, Tone 0 to Tone 3, all RAW, followed by Reset map.

4. Select Tone 0 and turn E3 once right. It reads BASS. Press K3; the footer reads APPLIED. Checkpoint: play and stop. C still plays as MIDI 60 because it lies inside the default Bass register (24 to 60), so this mapping alone does not change the sound.

5. Select Tone 2 and turn E3 twice right so it reads INNER1. Press K3. Tone 1 (D) stays RAW.

6. Select Tone 3 and turn E3 five times right so it reads TOP. Press K3.

7. Turn E1 to return to the Voice leading list. Select Register with E2 and press K3. The Register list opens: Role (the first role is Bass), Low, High, Centre, Preferred leap, Strict leap.

8. Select High with E2 and turn E3 five times left. High reads 55. Press K3.

9. Press Play and listen to two loops, then press Stop. The Bass register now ends at 55, so 60 no longer fits and C plays as MIDI 48 (C2), the nearest C inside it. D stays at MIDI 62 because it is RAW. E and F are placed in their Inner 1 and Top registers. Open Result straight away (next step) to see each pitch.

10. Read the result: turn E1 to return to the Voice leading list, select Result and press K3, then select Step and turn E3 to steps 1, 3 and 4. Each shows its planned and sent pitch.

A repeated mapped value uses one pitch for the whole harmonic frame: if the phrase were C D C F, both Cs would sound as MIDI 48. If a role's range leaves no legal placement for a mapped note, Result shows NO VOICING RANGE and that note is silent. See [Captured Harmony range failure and fallback](#harmony/harmony-range-failure-and-fallback).

routes.source_title: Build the recording: Block chords, then Revoice
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1, range 1–16. Set Note MIDI 48, Vel 80, Len 2 steps, Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th; add trigs at 1, 5, 9 and 13 with roots MIDI 48, 45, 53 and 55 (C, A, F and G). Use the expandable Shared channel, Song and grid controls guide for navigation and coordinates.

1. Build Song slot 1 at length 32 with Harmony Mode Off. Play the four chords twice to establish their written root-position voicing.

2. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2; keep length 32. Open Channel tasks > Harmony. Select Mode with E2, choose REVOICE with E3 and press K3. Select Register with E2 and press K3; select Bass Mode with E2, choose ROOT with E3 and apply as the page indicates.

3. Play both slots, then stop and select slot 1 to restore Harmony Off.

routes.source_title: Map an external keyboard through the scale’s rotated degrees
routes.expected_visible_text:
Goal: compare the same incoming MIDI keys with Honour scale rotations Off and On. Map scale to white keys places the selected scale on the keyboard’s white keys; the Honour switches control whether the Scale Editor’s degree, rotation and transpose settings affect that mapping.

1. Baseline: in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, set Map scale to white keys On. In the Scale Editor select C natural minor, set degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2. Set Honour scale degree On, Honour scale rotations Off and Honour scale transpose Off. Play MIDI keys 60 through 72 chromatically at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 70, 70, 72, 72, 74.

2. Rotation comparison: turn Honour scale rotations On and replay MIDI keys 60 through 72 at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 58, 58, 60, 60, 74. The last two scale positions are an octave lower.

routes.source_title: Apply scale rotation and global transpose to every keyboard key
routes.expected_visible_text:
Goal: compare the same incoming MIDI keys with Honour scale transpose Off and On. Map scale to white keys lays the selected scale on white keys; each Honour switch controls whether its named Scale Editor transformation participates.

1. Baseline: in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, set Map scale to white keys On. In the Scale Editor select C natural minor, set degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2. Set Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations On, and Honour scale transpose Off. Play MIDI keys 60 through 72 chromatically at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 58, 58, 60, 60, 74.

2. Transpose comparison: turn Honour scale transpose On and replay the same keys at velocity 90. Output: 64, 65, 65, 67, 67, 69, 70, 70, 60, 60, 62, 62, 76. Every mapped note is two semitones higher.

routes.source_title: Copy a slot before editing
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: slot 1 holds a section you want to keep, for example the four-note motif C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Playback is stopped and the Song editor is open (Song, grid (6,8)).

1. Hold slot 1 at (1,1). While holding it, press an empty slot, slot 2 at (2,1). Release both. Slot 2 changes from dim to mid-bright: it is a full copy and slot 1 is untouched. Copying overwrites the destination, so choose an empty one.

2. Tap slot 2 at (2,1). It turns bright (selected) and slot 1 drops to mid-bright.

3. Edit the variation while stopped: press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Only slot 2 changes. (Changing a mask instead works too; either edit stays in the selected slot.)

4. Press Play (1,8). Slot 2 plays the motif an octave higher (72, 74, 76, 77); with Song mode On playback then carries on to slot 1, so press Stop when you have heard enough. Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play: the original section still plays 60, 62, 64, 65. Tap slot 2 to compare.

The destination is a full copy, so editing it never changes the original. To erase a slot you no longer need, hold an empty slot and press the slot to clear. There is no undo.
