The captured example [Copy a slot, then change the copy](#song-mode-operations/song-copy-and-compare) shows steps 1 to 3 (the copy and the octave edit); to hear slot 1 and slot 2 compare, follow [Build two song groups](#song-mode-operations/song-build-two-groups), which plays the copies. The captured example [Read Song slot lights](#button-indicators/song-slot-light-states) shows the lights for a copy and for the erase.

routes.source_title: Copy a Song slot, then raise the copy by one octave
routes.expected_visible_text:
1. Stop playback. In Song view, set the song length to two steps and copy slot 1 into slot 2. Select slot 2 at (2,1) before channel editing.
2. Select channel 1 and raise its octave for slot 2.
3. Compare the copied slot’s stored motif and octave setting with slot 1.
Outcome: Slot 2 begins as a copy of slot 1, then its channel octave is set to +1.

routes.source_title: Set Window 0
routes.expected_visible_text:
Musical purpose: stop one channel’s extra notes landing on another channel’s anchor, for example hi-hat additions that never double the kick. Interlock changes only the follower’s additions. Anchors on both channels always play.

Starting point: Foundation is on for two channels, both with 8-step loops. Channel 1 (the follower, MIDI channel 1) has anchor Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) and Pattern 2 (a C on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (the leader, MIDI channel 2) has anchor Pattern 3, a single trig on step 5; channel 1 has no leader, and its grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

1. Select channel 1 on the grid (button (1,1)). Turn E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3.
2. Select Rhythm and press K3, then select Interlock (the last row) and press K3. The Interlock list opens: Leader OFF, Window 0, Status.
3. Select Leader and turn E3 once right. Leader reads CH02. A channel cannot follow itself, so CH01 is not offered.
4. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED, Window stays 0 and Status reads ON. Step 5 goes dark on the channel 1 grid: Pattern 2’s addition starts exactly on the leader’s anchor and is removed. Steps 1 to 4 and step 7 stay lit.
5. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to two loops, then press Stop. Channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and step 7, and channel 2 plays its anchor on step 5; nothing from channel 1 sounds on step 5.
6. Select Window and turn E3 twice right. Window reads 2.
7. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Step 7 also goes dark, because it is two steps from the leader’s anchor on step 5, and only steps 1 to 4 remain on channel 1; if you apply while playing, the footer reads NEXT CYCLE and the change starts at the next loop.

Window 0 removes only additions that start with a leader anchor. Each step of Window widens the gap by one follower step, up to 4.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured Interlock Leader and Window workflow](#interlock/interlock-leader-window).

routes.source_title: Hear every note restricted
routes.expected_visible_text:
Use this option to keep generated, random or merged material consonant: with Lock all to pent. On, every note lands on the five-note version of the scale. The seven-note walk below is a diagnostic rather than a phrase, so you can hear exactly which degrees are replaced. Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major.

1. Build seven degrees. Press Pattern (5,8), select pattern 1 (1,1) and tap trigs on steps 5, 6 and 7 at (5,4), (6,4) and (7,4). Press Pattern (5,8) again for the note page and tap (5,3), (6,2) and (7,1) to put steps 5 to 7 on degrees V, VI and VII: steps 1 to 7 now form a rising diagonal.

2. Set the range. Press Channel (3,8), hold step 1 (1,4), tap step 7 (7,4) and release both. Tap Play (1,8) and listen: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71. Tap Play to stop.

3. Restrict the notes. Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock all to pent. and turn E3 to On. Close the menu and tap Play: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 69, 72. F falls to E and B rises to C because only C D E G A are allowed. Tap Play to stop.

4. Change the scale. Open the Scale Editor (4,8), turn E2 to Scale, then turn E3 to Minor (natural minor). Release all grid keys and press K3 to apply the draft, then return to Channel (3,8). Play again: the five-note selection follows the new scale. Minor gives 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 70.

5. Turn the option Off in PARAMS > MOSAIC to restore all seven degrees of the current scale.

routes.source_title: Compare merged notes with and without the filter
routes.expected_visible_text:
Lock merged to pent. is On by default. Merge modes can produce notes that no pattern contains, such as an average between two degrees; this option snaps those results onto the five-note version of the scale. Use this recipe to hear the difference.

Starting point: channel 1 is empty and the scale is C major.

1. Build pattern 1 on degrees I, III, V, VII (C E G B) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 on III, V, VII, I (E G B C) on steps 1 to 4, as in Build a phrase, and pattern 3 as a velocity source (four trigs on steps 1 to 4, never assigned to the channel). Both note patterns have a trig on all four steps.

2. Assign both patterns to channel 1 with (1,2) and (2,2).

3. Choose the merge modes. Both patterns trig on the same steps, and the default trig merge, Skip, silences steps that trig in more than one pattern, so set the trig merge to All: press the trig merge button (14,8) until Channel tasks > Merge modes shows ALL. Check that the note merge reads AVERAGE; the average of each pair of degrees is II, IV, VI, IV (D, F, A, F).

4. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Tap Play: 62, 65, 69, 65 (D, F, A, F). Tap Play to stop.

5. Turn Lock merged to pent. On and play again: 62, 64, 69, 64. The two F notes become E, because F is not in the pentatonic.

routes.source_title: Compare random notes with and without the filter
routes.expected_visible_text:
Lock random to pent. is On by default. This recipe lets you hear what it does by switching it Off and On with Random Note at 4. Random Note chooses its offsets at random, so listen to several loops: a short run may not include every note.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major; no Trig params slot is assigned yet.

1. Assign Random Note. Select channel 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. Press K2 to open the parameter list, turn E3 to Random Note, press K3 to assign it to the first slot and press K2 to return. The slot reads 0 and the pattern still plays C, D, E, F.

2. Set the amount. With the Random Note slot selected (E2), turn E3 four detents right to 4. Each note is now offset by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees at random. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Close the menu, tap Play and listen to several loops: F and B may join the random notes, but neither is guaranteed to appear in a short run. Tap Play to stop.

4. Turn Lock random to pent. On and play several loops again. The random notes now stay on C, D, E, G and A. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note, so a plain F in the pattern can still sound. The random stream is not reset between the two runs, so the two runs will not start with the same notes; compare which notes occur, not the order.

routes.source_title: Use a channel octave for a bass line and a local octave exception
routes.expected_visible_text:
Start with a routed four-note C–D–E–F phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65), pattern 1 on steps 1–4, stopped. Keep the line low but lift its second note.

1. On Channel, tap octave −2 at (8,8). Play and stop: the line moves down two octaves. The octave buttons (8,8) through (12,8) select −2, −1, 0, +1, +2.
2. Hold step 2 at (2,4), tap −1 at (9,8) and release. Play and stop: only the second note is one octave higher than its neighbours. A local −1 replaces the channel −2; it is not added to it.
3. Hold step 2 and press K2, then release. The step inherits −2 again.
4. Hold step 2 and tap 0 at (10,8), then release. This explicit zero plays the written register on step 2. Clear it with held-step K2 to restore the bass register.

Outcome: an octave exception changes one step, and clearing restores the channel register. Compare the authentic results at [Octave Locks](#octave-locks).

routes.source_title: Distinguish an explicit zero transpose lock from inheritance
routes.expected_visible_text:
Start with the four-note C–D–E–F melody. Setup A: on the Scale page, set global transpose to +4. Setup B: hold scale-track step 2, set its transpose lock to 0 with the fader, then release it. The zero lock persists until the next lock or the scale-track wrap. Now compare the lock on step 1 with inheritance.

1. Hold scale-track step 1 and move its transpose lock to 0 using the fader. The held-step tooltip shows zero: this is a chosen value, not an empty lock.
2. Release the step. Global +4 remains on the fader, while the step’s zero replaces it when that step is reached.
3. Hold step 1 and press K2 to clear only that lock, then release. Step 1 follows global +4; the separate zero lock at step 2 remains and restores the written pitch from step 2 onwards.

Outcome: clearing a zero lock restores inheritance; it does not erase the next step’s lock. See [Transposition Locks](#transposition-locks) for the direct-tap comparison.

routes.source_title: Comparing the Loop Alignment
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: the numbered setup in Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops is complete and playback is stopped. Both channels run at the same rate. At 90 BPM and Rate /1 one step is a sixth of a second, so you can count 12 steps in two seconds.

1. Press Play and count steps. Channel 1 plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 and then repeats, so it completes three phrases in 12 steps. Channel 2 plays MIDI 79, 81, 79 and repeats, so it completes four phrases in the same 12 steps.

2. Listen at step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together. This same pitch pair also occurs at step 9, so it is not unique. Count phrase starts: after step 1, the two loops next realign at step 13. On step 4, channel 1 plays MIDI 65 while channel 2 starts a new phrase with MIDI 79.

3. Listen at step 13, two seconds after step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together again, and the pattern repeats every 12 steps. Press Stop when you have heard the alignment.

4. Optional extra check, unrelated to the alignment: with both channels playing, try a reversed range on channel 1. Hold step 4 as the start, press step 2 as the end and release both. The reversed range is rejected with a message, the ranges stay 1–4 and 1–3, and neither phrase changes timing.

routes.source_title: Comparing Song Boundary Resets
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: the two looping channels above (channel 1 range 1–4, channel 2 range 1–3), with Song slot 1 holding them and playback stopped. Song mode is On by default, so the slots play in turn, and Reset on song seq change (PARAMS > MOSAIC) is On by default while Reset on pattern repeat is Off. This comparison hears how the first option changes both channels at a slot boundary.

1. Set slot 1 to ten steps before copying it. Open the Song Editor and tap slot 1 at (1,1). On the length fader, tap (2,7) to jump to 1, then tap (8,7) nine times to reach 10. This length belongs to the selected slot and applies to both its channels. Ten is not a multiple of 4 or 3, so each channel is part-way through its loop when the slot ends.

2. Copy the ten-step slot. Hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1), then release slot 1. Slot 2 inherits slot 1's patterns and length 10. Leave slot 3 empty and select slot 1 again: the two ten-step sections will play in turn.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and check that Reset on song seq change reads On. Play both slots. At the start of slot 2 both channels restart from step 1: channel 1 plays MIDI 60 and channel 2 plays MIDI 79. The 4-against-3 pattern starts again from the beginning in every slot. Press Stop.

4. Set Reset on song seq change to Off and play both slots again. Now neither channel restarts: at the start of slot 2 channel 1 continues with MIDI 64, the third note of its phrase (10 steps is two phrases and two steps), and channel 2 continues with MIDI 81, the second note of its phrase (10 steps is three phrases and one step). The two channels no longer meet at the slot boundary. Press Stop.

5. Set Reset on song seq change back to On to restore the default.

Use Off when you want the 12-step relationship to carry across slots without a restart; use On when each slot should begin with both loops on their first step.

routes.source_title: Run two channels at different lengths
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: two channels with audible notes. Give each channel a voice (for example Oilcan 1 on channel 1 and Polyperc 1 on channel 2, or any two MIDI outputs) and set Note, Vel and Len on each channel's Masks page as in Make your first loop (a channel needs at least one audible note to be heard).

Enter the two patterns. Tap Pattern (5,8) for the Trig view. In pattern 1 tap steps (1,4), (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4): a drum pattern with trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. In pattern 2 tap steps (1,4), (3,4) and (4,4): a short figure with trigs on steps 1, 3 and 4.

1. Channel 1: tap (1,1) and assign pattern 1 at (1,2). Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)), tap step 16 ((16,4)), then release step 1. Steps 1-16 on row 4 are now brighter.

2. Channel 2: tap (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 ((5,4)), then release step 1. On this channel only steps 1-5 are brighter.

3. Tap Play at (1,8). The drum channel repeats every 16 steps (four hits per bar) and the figure repeats every 5 steps, so its three notes slide across the drum hits. Listen for the figure landing on a different drum beat each bar.

4. Keep listening until the start of drum bar 6. After 80 steps (five drum bars, sixteen figure passes) both channels start together again. 80 is the first step count that both 16 and 5 divide. Tap Play again to stop.

If the song moves to another song pattern, channels are reset together while Reset at Song Sequence Change (on by default) is enabled, so the 80-step cycle only completes while the same song pattern keeps playing. Use the Options page to change how channels of different length behave. The captured example [Play sixteen steps against five](#loops-that-meet/loops-sixteen-against-five) builds this setup and plays the 80 steps until both channels start together again. The captured example "Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed" shows the range gesture and what happens when the end comes before the start.

routes.source_title: Listening extension: sixteen steps against twelve
routes.expected_visible_text:
Start from an empty independent project at 90 BPM and Rate /1, with Song mode off so the channel loops run continuously. This is the separate Sixteen steps against twelve recording.

1. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–16. In Masks, set channel Vel 80 and Len 1/2. Add trigs on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15. Set their Note masks to MIDI 36, 37, 36, 37 and 38 respectively.
2. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 2 and set its range to steps 1–12. In Masks, set channel Vel 60 and Len 1/2. Add trigs on steps 1, 4, 7 and 10. Set their Note masks to MIDI 48, 55, 52 and 55 respectively. Keep Snap note masks to scale Off so the drum note numbers stay unchanged.
3. Press Play. The loops meet every forty-eight steps: listen for the bass phrase landing differently against the drums in bars 2 and 3, then both returning to their first step at the beginning of bar 4.
4. Stop after four bars to match the recording. The bass ends four steps into its next twelve-step loop. This setup has different notes, sounds and loop lengths from the four-against-three lesson; keep the projects separate.

routes.source_title: Play a minor scale on the white keys
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: a MIDI keyboard is connected to Mosaic's MIDI input on port 1, channel 1 has a device selected (it plays through the test or your own synth) and the scale is C major. The norns names MIDI 60 as C3, so the key you call middle C sounds 60.

1. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, turn E2 to Map scale to white keys and turn E3 to On. Play the white keys from C to C: C major, 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71, 72, the same pitches as before. Each black key repeats the white key above it.

2. Open the Scale Editor (4,8). Turn E2 to Scale, turn E3 to natural minor and press K3 to apply it. Return to the Channel editor (3,8).

3. Play C to C on the white keys again: 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72. The keyboard keeps its layout while the scale underneath it has changed.

routes.source_title: Contrast inherited velocity with explicit zero and a cleared exception
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: channel 1’s phrase has active trigs on steps 1 and 2.

1. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Select Vel with E2. With no step held, turn E3 to 50 for the channel default.
2. Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 clockwise to 90 and release. This exception makes the first hit louder.
3. Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 anticlockwise to 0 and release. Its note is silent while the first hit keeps the 90 accent. Play and stop to compare them.
4. Hold step 2 again, press K2 and release. It now inherits the default 50; the accent on step 1 remains.

Outcome: X inherits the channel velocity; explicit 0 silences a step. Clearing one exception restores its default without erasing its neighbour.

routes.source_title: Try a different ending for a four-note melody
routes.expected_visible_text:
Goal: change only the last note so the same four-step melody can resolve to a different ending; steps 1–3 remain fixed.

Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop. Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with channel defaults Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, so it repeats one note four times. The Masks screen shows the note name for the value you are editing, and one detent of E3 moves one MIDI note, so turn E3 until the screen reads the name given below instead of counting. Norns shows MIDI 60 as C3, so 72 is C4, 74 is D4, 76 is E4 and 79 is G4.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and, with no step held, the Note row shows the channel default, C3.

2. Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)). The header gains ST01, which means edits now apply to that step only. Turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (12 detents), then release the step.

3. Hold step 2 (2,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads D4 (14 detents) and release the step.

4. Hold step 3 (3,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads G4 (19 detents) and release the step.

5. Hold step 4 (4,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads E4 (16 detents) and release the step. After each release the screen goes back to the channel default, C3; each step you set keeps its own note.

6. Tap Play at (1,8). The loop plays C4, D4, G4, E4 (72, 74, 79, 76). Tap Play again to stop.

7. Hold step 4 and turn E3 left until the screen reads D4 (two detents). Release the step and tap Play: the phrase now ends C4, D4, G4, D4. Only step 4 changed; steps 1-3 keep their masks. Tap Play to stop.

8. To end on the root instead, hold step 4 and turn E3 left until the screen reads C4 (two more detents). Release the step and tap Play: the phrase is C4, D4, G4, C4.

All of these notes are in the default C major scale, so scale snapping leaves them unchanged. A note outside the scale is moved onto it. The captured example "Change the ending of a four-note melody" runs steps 1 to 8 on the four-note loop and shows the MIDI strip after each change (its pattern keeps its own velocities, so the recipe's Vel 80 is not repeated there); "Set channel and step note masks" shows the same hold-and-turn gestures on a different loop.

routes.source_title: Add a ghost note before an accent
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop, with channel default Vel 80. A ghost note is a very quiet note played just before a louder one; it makes the louder note feel pushed.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Turn E2 to Vel. With no step held the screen reads 80, the channel default.

2. Hold step 3 (grid (3,4)) and turn E3 right until the screen reads 100. Release the step. Step 3 is now the accent.

3. Hold step 2 (2,4) and turn E3 left until the screen reads 35. Release the step. Step 2 is the ghost note.

4. Tap Play at (1,8). The velocities are 80, 35, 100, 80: a soft tap on step 2 leads into the loud step 3. Tap Play again to stop.

The [captured screen/grid example, Set a ghost note and an accent](#masks/mask-ghost-note) shows the same 80, 35, 100, 80 MIDI velocities over C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65). It shows the exact mask edits from this recipe.
Listen to the [separate Oilcan comparison, Adding a Ghost Note](#recording/ghost-note-comparison): bars 1 and 2 play the main hits; bars 3 and 4 add MIDI 38 at velocity 35 on step 12 before the MIDI 37 accent. This recording uses a different four-bar drum arrangement, not the C, D, E, F loop above.
To make the ghost note come and go, continue with [Make the ghost note intermittent](#masks/recipe/3).

routes.source_title: Make the ghost note intermittent
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: the ghost-note loop from Add a ghost note before an accent (step 2 at velocity 35, step 3 at 100). Velocity decides how loud a note is; Trig Probability decides whether the trig plays at all. At 50, some loop passes include the ghost note and some omit it; judge over several passes, not from one fixed sequence.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. The screen shows all ten slots at once. A slot that has no parameter assigned yet is an empty slot.

2. Turn E2 to the first empty slot. E2 stops at slot 1 and at slot 10.

3. Press K2, turn E3 until Trig Probability appears, press K3 to assign it and press K2 to return to slot selection. The slot now carries Trig Probability.

4. Hold step 2 (grid (2,4)) and turn E3 until the screen reads 50. Release the step. Step 2 now has its own probability of 50; the other steps use the channel default and still play every time.

5. Tap Play at (1,8) and listen over several passes: the ghost note sounds on about half of them and the other three notes never drop out. Tap Play again to stop.

6. To remove the exception, hold step 2 on Trig params and press K2. This clears every parameter lock on that step.

Steps 1 to 3 (moving to an empty slot and assigning Trig Probability) are shown screen by screen in the captured example "Turn chance into explicit rests".

routes.source_title: Add chord voices over a bass
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: keep the four-step loop from [Make your first loop](#getting-started) on channel 1 and use channel 2 for the chord. The bass device can be monophonic; channel 2 needs a polyphonic device because one step plays several notes together. The audio example "A bass with room above it" below plays the same idea with Polyperc 1 for the bass and Doubledecker for the chords; its notes and levels differ from the values used here.

Set up the bass on channel 1.

1. Tap (1,1) to select channel 1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3.

2. With no step held, set Note to C2 (MIDI 48), Vel to 70 and Len to 1/2. Channel 1 now plays bass notes on steps 1-4.

Set up the chord channel.

3. Tap (2,1) to select channel 2. Open Channel tasks, choose Device and pick a polyphonic voice; press K3 to apply it.

4. Assign pattern 1 to channel 2: tap pattern slot (1,2).

5. Set channel 2 to the same four steps: hold step 1 (1,4), tap step 4 (4,4), then release step 1.

6. On Masks, with no step held, set channel 2's Note to C3 (MIDI 60), Vel to 60 and Len to 1/2. Checkpoint: it now plays single notes over the bass. If the chord channel is silent later, verify it has a polyphonic device assigned.

Add the chord voices.

7. Turn E2 to Chd1 and, with no step held, turn E3 two detents to 3rd. Every step adds the scale third above its root: 64.

8. Turn E2 to Chd2 and turn E3 four detents to 5th. Every step adds the scale fifth: 67.

9. Result check: tap Play at (1,8). Channel 2 plays C3, E3 and G3 (60, 64, 67) together on every step over bass C2 (48). If only C3 sounds, check that Chd1 is 3rd and Chd2 is 5th and that the channel uses a polyphonic device. Tap Play again to stop.

Change the voicing.

10. Turn E2 to Chd3 and set 6th (five detents): the chord adds A (69). Hold a single step and change a Chd row to give only that step a different voicing.

Chd values are scale intervals above the root, not MIDI note numbers. In another scale the same 3rd and 5th give that scale's intervals. The captured example "Set chord masks" shows each Chd edit and the MIDI notes it produces.

routes.source_title: Contrast inherited velocity with explicit zero and a cleared exception
routes.expected_visible_text:
1. Set the channel Vel mask to 50 and add a step-1 accent at 90.
2. Hold step 2 and set Vel to 0; read zero while held, then release and inspect the phrase with step 2 silent.
3. Hold step 2, press K2 and release it; the step inherits 50 again while the step-1 accent remains.
Outcome: X inherits the channel velocity; an explicit 0 silences the step. Clearing the step mask restores 50 without erasing the 90 accent.

routes.source_title: Set a two-cycle Build phrase
routes.expected_visible_text:
Musical purpose: build a part over two loops. Loop 1 plays the anchor line with one extra note. Loop 2 plays the same line with both extra notes.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop at 90 BPM with the default Rate /1, so each step is one sixteenth note (one sixth of a second). Pattern 1 holds C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97). Pattern 2 holds a C on steps 5 and 7, and both patterns are assigned to the channel. Strategy is SKIP.

1. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3. The Merge Shape list opens: Strategy, Rhythm, Phrase, Pitch, Result.
2. Select Rhythm with E2 and press K3. The Rhythm list opens with Anchor on the first row.
3. Turn E3 once so Anchor reads 01, then press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Pattern 1 is now the anchor, so its four trigs always play.
4. Turn E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until it reads FOUNDATION (or press grid (14,8) until it does). Active reads FOUNDATION. The channel grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7: four anchors and two possible additions.
5. Return to Merge Shape. Select Phrase with E2 and press K3. The Phrase list opens: Cycles, Shape, Variation.
6. Select Cycles and turn E3 once right. Cycles reads 2 and two Cycle rows appear.
7. Select Shape and turn E3 once right, from FLAT to BUILD. Cycle 1 reads 50 and Cycle 2 reads 100, so the first loop admits half of the additions and the second loop admits all of them.
8. Press K3 on a value row. The footer reads APPLIED.
9. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to four loops, then press Stop. Loop 1 plays C D E F and one extra C on step 7; loop 2 plays C D E F and extra Cs on steps 5 and 7; then the two loops repeat. The extra notes play at velocity 70, quieter than the anchors.

What each loop plays (an added C is shown as +C):

Loop 1: steps 1 to 4 C D E F, step 5 rest, step 7 +C.

Loop 2: steps 1 to 4 C D E F, step 5 +C, step 7 +C.

Listen for the loop-to-loop change: the extra C on step 5 is present in every second loop only.

To make the additions quieter or louder without changing how many play, change Add accent in Rhythm.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured two-cycle Build workflow](#merge-shape/foundation-two-cycle-build).

routes.source_title: Map an external keyboard through the scale’s rotated degrees
routes.expected_visible_text:
Goal: compare the same incoming MIDI keys with Honour scale rotations Off and On. Map scale to white keys places the selected scale on the keyboard’s white keys; the Honour switches control whether the Scale Editor’s degree, rotation and transpose settings affect that mapping.

1. Baseline: in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, set Map scale to white keys On. In the Scale Editor select C natural minor, set degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2. Set Honour scale degree On, Honour scale rotations Off and Honour scale transpose Off. Play MIDI keys 60 through 72 chromatically at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 70, 70, 72, 72, 74.

2. Rotation comparison: turn Honour scale rotations On and replay MIDI keys 60 through 72 at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 58, 58, 60, 60, 74. The last two scale positions are an octave lower.

routes.source_title: Apply scale rotation and global transpose to every keyboard key
routes.expected_visible_text:
Goal: compare the same incoming MIDI keys with Honour scale transpose Off and On. Map scale to white keys lays the selected scale on white keys; each Honour switch controls whether its named Scale Editor transformation participates.

1. Baseline: in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, set Map scale to white keys On. In the Scale Editor select C natural minor, set degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2. Set Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations On, and Honour scale transpose Off. Play MIDI keys 60 through 72 chromatically at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 58, 58, 60, 60, 74.

2. Transpose comparison: turn Honour scale transpose On and replay the same keys at velocity 90. Output: 64, 65, 65, 67, 67, 69, 70, 70, 60, 60, 62, 62, 76. Every mapped note is two semitones higher.

routes.source_title: Silence connected MIDI notes from Song view with the Channel panic gesture
routes.expected_visible_text:
Use this on a connected MIDI instrument when a note is stuck. The panic gesture sends note-release messages to connected MIDI outputs, but it does not stop the sequencer. The manual’s captured Output strip replays a recorded result; it does not send messages to your instrument.

1. Open Song at (6,8), so Channel is an inactive page button.
2. Hold Channel at (3,8) until the panic gesture fires, then release. The page remains Song.
3. A stuck MIDI note should stop; inspect the release messages in Output. The sequencer keeps running, so new notes may still play. Press Stop separately if you want silence to continue.

Use [Silence a sounding note](#midi-panic/panic-stops-sounding-note) for the long-note comparison. The other examples show the gesture from a silent project.

routes.source_title: Silence connected MIDI notes from Song view with the Pattern panic gesture
routes.expected_visible_text:
Use this on a connected MIDI instrument when a note is stuck. The panic gesture sends note-release messages to connected MIDI outputs, but it does not stop the sequencer. The manual’s captured Output strip replays a recorded result; it does not send messages to your instrument.

1. Open Song at (6,8), so Pattern is an inactive page button.
2. Hold Pattern at (5,8) until the panic gesture fires, then release. The page remains Song.
3. A stuck MIDI note should stop; inspect the release messages in Output. The sequencer keeps running, so new notes may still play. Press Stop separately if you want silence to continue.

Use [Silence a sounding note](#midi-panic/panic-stops-sounding-note) for the long-note comparison. The other examples show the gesture from a silent project.

routes.source_title: Prepare Mosaic for a live set
routes.expected_visible_text:
Goal: make an accidental tap safe, confirm the deliberate stop gestures, then leave automatic Song playback enabled.

1. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC.
2. Select Shift press to stop and turn E3 to On, so a stray tap cannot stop the sequencer.
3. Press K2, then K1, and start playback with Play/Stop at grid (1,8). A quick second tap is ignored, and so is a hold shorter than one second.
4. To stop, hold K1 and tap Play/Stop, or hold Play/Stop for one second or more. Shift press stop lists every stop gesture.
5. Leave Song mode On, its default, if the arrangement should advance on its own. [Decide whether a slow channel restarts](#reset-at-pattern-repeat/repeat-reset-policies) turns Song mode Off to show the difference, and [Set Song slot repetitions](#navigating-the-norns-display/song-slot-repeat-values) shows Song mode in Slot setup. The other option groups are described below.

routes.source_title: Make the recorded ghost-note comparison
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped and channel 1 selected. If Oilcan 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable `nb_oilcan` in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). The numbers 1–64 are step numbers across four bars: bar 1 is steps 1–16, bar 2 is 17–32, bar 3 is 33–48 and bar 4 is 49–64. For Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. These screens do not page.


Setup (steps 1 to 3 prepare the instrument; do them once).

1. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–64 (see Channel Length). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Set 90 BPM: open Song tasks, choose Tempo & feel, turn E3 to 90 and press K3.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, then return to Mosaic. MIDI 37 (C#1) is not in C major and would otherwise be snapped to a scale note. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign pattern 1 to the channel.


Main hits (steps 4 to 7 build and audition the bar without ghost notes).

4. Add the main hits. Open Pattern Trig on pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 in each bar: bar 1 uses 1, 5, 9, 13; bar 2 uses 17, 21, 25, 29; bar 3 uses 33, 37, 41, 45; bar 4 uses 49, 53, 57, 61. Sixteen trigs are lit.

5. Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, select Note and set MIDI 36 (C1), select Vel and set 90, select Len and set ½. All sixteen hits now play MIDI 36 at velocity 90.

6. Select Note. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release. Do the same for steps 13, 21, 29, 37, 45, 53 and 61, so that the second and fourth beat of each bar play MIDI 37.

routes.source_title: Snap anchors to a chord, then try Every 4
routes.expected_visible_text:
Musical purpose: land the strong notes of a line on the tones of a chord while the notes between them stay as written. Anchors snaps every anchor note. Every 4 snaps only steps 1 and 5 of an 8-step loop and leaves the rest of the line alone.

Terms: a Harmony group is a stored chord. Its Template count is how many tones the chord has, each Tone row sets that tone's offset from the root, and Group enabled lets other features use it. Structure moves a marked note to the nearest tone of an enabled group's chord.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop with Foundation on. Pattern 1 is the anchor (C D E F on steps 1 to 4, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Pattern 2 supplies additions: D (62) on step 5 and C (60) on step 7. If Foundation is not on yet, follow steps 1 to 4 of Set a two-cycle Build phrase first. Steps 1 to 3 build a group that holds the chord C E G; if you already have an enabled group with that chord, start at step 4.

1. Create the group: turn E1 for Channel tasks, select Harmony and press K3. Select Ensemble with E2 and press K3. Select Create group and press K3. Group 1 appears.

2. Set the chord: Select Template count and turn E3 twice right, so the chord has 3 tones. Select Tone 2 and turn E3 twice right. Select Tone 3 and turn E3 four times right. With the root, the offsets 2 and 4 are C E G in C major. Press K3 on a value row. The footer reads APPLIED.

3. Enable the group: press K2 to return to the Ensemble list. Select Members and press K3, select Group enabled, turn E3 once right to ON and press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Group 1 is enabled.

4. Open Structure: turn E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape and press K3. Select Pitch and press K3, then select Structure and press K3. The Structure list opens with Markers OFF.

5. Select Markers and turn E3 once right. Markers reads ANCHORS and a Chord group row appears showing 1, then press K3. The footer reads APPLIED.

6. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to two loops. The anchors C D E F sound as C C E E (MIDI 60, 60, 64, 64): D is equally near C and E and takes the lower one, and F is nearer E than G. The additions keep their written D on step 5 and C on step 7. Press Stop.

7. Now the contrast. Select Markers and turn E3 once right. Markers reads EVERY 4, so only steps 1 and 5 are markers. Press K3.

8. Press Play. Step 1 stays C. Step 5 is a marker too, so its D moves to the nearest chord tone, C (the lower tie). D on step 2 and F on step 4 are not markers any more and return to their own pitches. The line plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, 60 and 60 in each loop. Then press Stop.

Choosing Anchors snaps every anchor, and Every 4 snaps only the beats you choose. Deleting or disabling the group turns Markers OFF.

The captured version, [Captured Structure group and marker workflow](#structure/structure-anchor-chord-and-delete), covers steps 1 to 6 with Anchors and then deletes the group. Steps 7 and 8 are captured in [Mark every fourth step](#structure/structure-every-4-markers), which starts from the enabled C E G group with Foundation on and shows Markers set to Every 4 and the line playing 60, 62, 64, 65, 60, 60 in each loop.

routes.source_title: Play a copied Song slot a tone higher
routes.expected_visible_text:
This recipe changes the transposition fader on a copy of a slot, so the copy plays a tone higher while the original stays put. It is a different workflow from the captured example below, which shows the fader being pressed while a note is sounding.

Start with Song slot 1 holding a finished sequence, such as a four-note melody on MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, with playback stopped and Song mode at its default (On).

2. Hold slot 1 at (1, 1) and press slot 2 at (2, 1), then release both. Slot 2 now holds a copy of slot 1 (copying overwrites whatever slot 2 held).

3. Press slot 2 at (2, 1) to select it while stopped.

4. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.

routes.source_title: Brighten the last note with a cutoff lock
routes.expected_visible_text:
Start with a channel that has trigs on steps 1 to 4 (see Build a phrase), sends to a device that lists a controller you can hear on a filter, and is stopped. This recipe uses CC 74, the usual filter cutoff controller: a generic CC device lists it as CC 74, and a device whose configuration names it shows it as Cutoff. The scenes on this page use CC 1 the same way.
1. Open Trig params: turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params, press K3.
2. Turn E2 to slot 1, press K2, turn E3 to CC 74 (Cutoff), press K3 to assign it, then press K2 to return to the slot view.
3. With no step held, turn E3 to 40, the channel default: every step sends CC 74 = 40 before its note.
4. Hold step 4, the last trig, and turn E3 to 100 (the cell shows 100 and the L marker). Release step 4 and the cell shows 40 again.
5. Press Play. Steps 1 to 3 sound with cutoff 40 and step 4 sends CC 74 = 100 just before its note, so the last note of each loop is brighter.
6. To remove the accent, hold step 4 and press K2.
On this page, the scene Lock a value, then clear just that step shows the same gestures with Fixed Note, the MIDI strip of Use the first and last Trig params slots shows CC values arriving just before their notes, and Keep a stored value while locking a step shows one locked CC value ahead of a step's note while the other steps send the stored value. For a smooth rise instead of a jump, see Param Slides.

routes.source_title: Hear automation on rests
routes.expected_visible_text:
Start stopped with channel 1 routed to a CC-responsive instrument or MIDI monitor, pattern 1 assigned over steps 1–4 and a trig on every step. Assign CC 1 to a Trig params slot. A trigless lock is a step-local parameter value on a step with no trig: it can move a filter or other CC-controlled parameter through a silent step.

1. Hold steps 1–4 in turn and set CC 1 to 24, 48, 72 and 96 with E3; release each step.
2. Open Pattern (5,8), select pattern 1 and remove the trig on step 3 at (3,4). Return to Channel (3,8). Editing a pattern affects every channel assigned that pattern.
3. Play and stop. Trigless locks is On by default: step 3 is silent but still sends CC 1 = 72.
4. Tap K1, open PARAMS → MOSAIC, select Trigless locks and set Off with E3. Return, play and stop: CC 1 sends 24, 48 and 96, skipping 72.
5. Restore On if the parameter should move through rests. A Trig probability of 0 suppresses a note without deleting its trig, so its locks are still sent in either setting.

The two visual examples add channel 2 as a timing reference using the same pattern. It follows pattern edits too: removing step 3 removes its E note on both channels. Channel 1’s probability locks remain local to channel 1. An audible filter comparison requires a receiver mapped to CC 1; these examples demonstrate the MIDI values.

routes.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps on the example MIDI device with Merge Shape set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, on steps 1 to 4) is the protected Anchor and pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) offers additions; both are assigned. Add amount is 100 and Add accent 70, so all candidate additions are allowed and sound at 70 percent of their velocity. The Phrase settings are still at their defaults, the norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

routes.source_title: Let each fragment keep its source notes
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays through the example MIDI device on an 8-step loop at 90 BPM, rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6. Both patterns are assigned to channel 1 and Strategy is still SKIP. Merge modes is open for channel 1. In this scene a Seed makes a repeatable draw of which pattern each fragment comes from: the same seed always gives the same choice.

routes.source_title: Let the channel beat the global setting
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. On enables full scale mapping; Off disables it. An absent step lock uses the channel, and channel X uses the global option. An explicitly stored step X skips the channel and uses the global option directly; clearing it with K2 restores channel inheritance. In the state lists, X without a stored step lock means no exception; explicit step X is named separately. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / Off / On. The global Off is inherited by the channel, step 1 is Off and step 2 is On, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

routes.source_title: Let the channel inherit the global setting
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. On enables full scale mapping; Off disables it. An absent step lock uses the channel, and channel X uses the global option. An explicitly stored step X skips the channel and uses the global option directly; clearing it with K2 restores channel inheritance. In the state lists, X without a stored step lock means no exception; explicit step X is named separately. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: On / Off / X / On. The channel Off beats the global On and step 2 has its own On lock, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

routes.source_title: Choose which note masks follow the scale
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1; both are already set in the scale editor. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Snap note masks to scale is On, while Quantise note masks (the global full-quantisation option) and Lock merged to pent. are Off. With Snap alone the masks play as written, 60, 64, 69, 71 in the MIDI strip, because Degree and Rotation affect masks only under full quantisation. On enables full scale mapping; Off disables it. An absent step lock uses the channel, and channel X uses the global option. An explicitly stored step X skips the channel and uses the global option directly; clearing it with K2 restores channel inheritance. In the state lists, X without a stored step lock means no exception; explicit step X is named separately. Each step below lists the state as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / X / X.

routes.source_title: Move between parameter locks
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a device with MIDI CCs, at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so one step lasts a sixth of a second. PARAMS is open on the device's CC 1 control at its stored value, 63, set in PARAMS > MOSAIC. CC 1 is not assigned to a Trig params slot yet, and parameter slides are off.

routes.source_title: Share a voicing while keeping each channel’s rhythm
routes.caption: Four channels play through the example MIDI device, each on its own MIDI channel (1 to 4) with its own sparse rhythm: channel 1 plays the four-step phrase, channel 2 steps 1 and 3, channel 3 steps 2 and 4 and channel 4 step 4. Scale slot 1 (C major) is applied, Harmony is Off on every channel and no scale or octave locks are set, so each channel plays its own written pitches. A Harmony Ensemble group lets several channels share one chord: each member gets a role (Bass, Inner or Top), keeps its own rhythm, and takes its pitch from the group's shared voicing. The norns shows the Device page of channel 4.

routes.source_title: See a failed voicing and choose a fallback
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on MIDI channel 1: C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 at 90 BPM, rate /1. Harmony is Off with its default registers and Failure fallback SILENCE. Playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page. This scene shows what happens when a register leaves no room for a note, as it can after you shift a voice into an unusual range.

routes.source_title: Place two voices smoothly
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1 to 4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through the example MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (rate /1). Each step is a single voice: no chord notes are set and Harmony is Off. Playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

routes.source_title: Inspect a step and return
routes.caption: A new empty project that has just started: stopped, Record off, channel 1 selected and no step held. The Channel editor is showing: its header reads NOTE MASKS CH01. The first step visits the page keys before you hold a step.

routes.source_title: Leave room around a leader’s anchors
routes.caption: Two 8-step channels play at 90 BPM through the example MIDI device. Channel 1 (MIDI channel 1) has pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and pattern 2 (steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has pattern 3, a single trig on step 5, as its Foundation anchor. Channel 1 has no Interlock leader yet. The norns shows channel 1's Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

routes.source_title: Apply the scale transpose to live input
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. This independent example begins with Degree and Rotation already enabled; it does not continue a previous project. Map scale to white keys is On and the scale is C natural minor, with degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2 set in the Scale Editor. Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations are On and Honour scale transpose is Off, so the white keys C3 to C4 play 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 58, 60, 74.

routes.source_title: Start from the chosen scale degree
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Map scale to white keys and the three Honour switches are Off, and the Scale Editor is on C major.

routes.source_title: Rotate the keyboard voicing
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Map scale to white keys is On and the scale is C natural minor. The Scale Editor holds degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2, and Honour scale degree is On, so the white keys C3 to C4 play 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72, 74. Honour scale rotations and Honour scale transpose are Off.

routes.source_title: Let a keyboard follow the scale
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on the example MIDI device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4. The scale is C major, a MIDI keyboard is connected on port 1 and Map scale to white keys is off, its default. The sequencer is stopped, so the keyboard plays the channel's output directly. The norns shows the Device page.

routes.source_title: Carry a slide across the loop boundary
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Wrap param slides is Off, and nothing is locked yet.

routes.source_title: Compare note-length merge modes
routes.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are both assigned to channel 1, with the same trigs on the same steps: pattern 1's notes are 2 steps long and pattern 2's are 4 steps long. Length merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8). Length merge is set with K1 (shift) held, which turns the velocity merge button (16,8) into the length button.

routes.source_title: Slide only one source lock
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a device with MIDI CCs, at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so one step lasts a sixth of a second. PARAMS is open on the device's CC 1 control at its stored value, 63, set in PARAMS > MOSAIC. CC 1 is not assigned to a Trig params slot yet, and parameter slides are off. This independent example enables the slide on step 1 only. Compare the whole-parameter glide separately at Param Slides; neither example requires the other’s project.

routes.source_title: Send lock values before their notes
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-note phrase through a MIDI device. The tempo is 130 BPM, the sequencer is stopped, the norns shows channel 1's Device screen and the PARAMS menu is closed. No trig params are assigned yet, so no CC values are sent.

routes.source_title: Play four steps against three
routes.caption: A new project with playback stopped, the default C major scale and Rate /1 (one step is a sixteenth note) on every channel. Channel 1 is set up and its Device page is open: it plays range 1-4, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, to its own MIDI output. Channel 2 is not set up yet.

routes.source_title: Play sixteen steps against five
routes.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device on OUT 1 and channel 2 to a second output, MIDI port 2 on MIDI channel 2. Each channel has its Masks defaults set so that every step sounds: channel 1 plays a low drum note, C1 (MIDI 36), at velocity 100 and channel 2 plays MIDI 72 at velocity 90, both half a step long. Channel 1's Masks screen is open. The Rate is /1 at 90 BPM, so one step lasts a sixth of a second, and playback is stopped.

routes.source_title: A loaded map follows the selected or fixed channel
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97 on steps 1 to 4. Channel 2 does not play yet; in the next step you set it up on MIDI port 2, channel 2 with the same pattern. A saved MIDI map is loaded with two relative controls that both accumulate: CC 20 edits the velocity mask of the selected channel and CC 21 edits the velocity mask of channel 2. Both velocity masks are Off (X) and the norns shows channel 1's Device page.

routes.source_title: Set chord masks
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and no masks are set. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Chd1. The four chord rows Chd1-Chd4 add voices above each step's root, and X means no voice.

routes.source_title: Set velocity and length masks
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Vel. The value reads X: there is no channel velocity mask, so every step plays the velocity it has in pattern 1. X means inherit.

routes.source_title: Set a ghost note and an accent
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Vel. The value reads X.

routes.source_title: Clear a note mask without clearing its neighbour
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. The Masks page (Channel tasks, then Masks) is open on Note. The channel's Note mask default is 67 (G3), step 1 has its own mask 72 and step 2 has 74, so the MIDI strip reads 72, 74, 67, 67.

routes.source_title: Change the ending of a four-note melody
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The value reads X.

routes.source_title: Unset the channel Note default
routes.caption: Starting point: pattern 1 plays C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Open Channel tasks → Masks → Note. With no step held, the Note value is X, so each step uses its merged pattern note.

routes.source_title: Set channel and step note masks
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

routes.source_title: Add and remove trig masks
routes.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 in an eight-step loop. Steps 1-4 hold four notes and steps 5-8 are empty. No masks are set. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The value reads X.

routes.source_title: Make a small CC move with Macro 1
routes.caption: In Matrix, choose Control 1, select Macro 1, and set its depth to 0.10. With Macro 1 at zero, the selected CC stays at 32.

routes.source_title: Route a macro and remove its depth
routes.caption: The norns matrix and toolkit mods are installed and enabled. Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a CC device with Rate /1, the sequencer is stopped, and the Matrix has no routes yet. The Device page for CH01 is showing.

routes.source_title: Undo, redo and replace a remembered edit
routes.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1. Nothing has been edited yet, so the channel's memory (its list of remembered edits) is empty.

routes.source_title: Merge two patterns
routes.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned. Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and pattern 2 has trigs on steps 1 and 2 (note C, velocity 100). The Merge modes screen is showing at 90 BPM with every merge mode at its default and playback stopped. The Patterns row reads 01 02: it only shows which patterns the channel plays, and turning E3 on it changes nothing. Assign patterns with the pattern slot buttons on the grid.

routes.source_title: Foundation and All: who decides the trigs
routes.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the example MIDI device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Both patterns are assigned, Add amount is 100 and Add accent is 70. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

routes.source_title: Skip and All on a step both patterns trig
routes.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the example MIDI device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100) has trigs on steps 3 and 7, so step 3 is a step both patterns trig. Both patterns are assigned. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 4 and 7.

routes.source_title: Lock merged notes to pentatonic: Off
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. Lock merged to pent. is at its default On. Only pattern 1 exists and is assigned to channel 1; patterns 2 and 3 are built in the next steps.

routes.source_title: Lock merged notes to pentatonic: On
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. Lock merged to pent. is at its default On. Only pattern 1 exists and is assigned to channel 1; patterns 2 and 3 are built in the next steps.

routes.source_title: Mute a channel and bring a running phrase back
routes.caption: Channel 1 sends to the example MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. No channel is muted, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.

routes.source_title: Remove the root without collapsing time
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Mute Chord Root. Chord Note Strum (1/2) and Chord Pattern (-> forward) are already assigned; Mute Chord Root is not.

routes.source_title: Keep a named project and recover it
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI notes 60, 62, 64 and 65. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. The project has never been saved under a name, so no new or newB file exists.

routes.source_title: Teach a relative MIDI controller
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped. A MIDI controller on input port 1, channel 1 is connected and sends relative CC 20: a value of 63 means one step down and 65 one step up. Nothing is mapped yet and the velocity mask is Off (X).

routes.source_title: Compare Average and Higher note merging
routes.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are assigned to channel 1, so channel 1 merges them. Pattern 1 plays scale degrees 1, 3, 5, 7 (C E G B) and pattern 2 plays degrees 3, 5, 7, 1 (E G B C). Note merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (15,8). Pentatonic snapping of merged notes is off: before you try this, tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Lock merged to pent. to Off. Left On (the default), merged notes snap to the five-note pentatonic version of the scale and you hear different pitches.

routes.source_title: Place one step in another octave
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI notes 60, 62, 64 and 65. The channel octave is 0 and no step has an octave lock. The Device page is showing. The octave buttons sit along the bottom row, (8,8) for -2 up to (12,8) for +2, with (10,8) the written octave.

routes.source_title: Read Output after selecting a channel
routes.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. The Output screen is open on channel 1. Playback has not started, so no note has played yet.

routes.source_title: Read the Output dashboard
routes.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1. Playback has not started, so no note has played yet.

routes.source_title: Read the latest note on Output
routes.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1 and playback has not started, so no note has played yet.

routes.source_title: Move a rhythm before committing
routes.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the fourth algorithm button (15,2) for Numeric. The Trig Algorithm screen marks Numeric as SELECTED. Numeric gives a sparse pattern, which makes shifts easy to see. The controls you will use on grid row 8 are Prime (16,8), Move left (10,8), Reset (11,8), Move right (12,8) and Cancel (14,8).

routes.source_title: Panic by holding Channel while on Song
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Pattern 1 is assigned to channel 1 over steps 1 to 4. The sequencer is stopped, so no note is sounding, and three MIDI ports are connected. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen; the next step opens Song.

routes.source_title: Panic by holding Pattern while on Song
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Pattern 1 is assigned to channel 1 over steps 1 to 4. The sequencer is stopped, so no note is sounding, and three MIDI ports are connected. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen; the next step opens Song.

routes.source_title: Copy notes and dynamics across the four step pages
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). A pattern has four step pages of 16 steps; here only page 1 has trigs and the Pattern editor has not been opened. Each channel plays a range of steps (start step to end step), which you will set at the end to hear one page at a time.

routes.source_title: Shape notes across the grid range
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Note the range buttons on row 8 are range-up (14,8), centre (15,8) and range-down (16,8). A press moves the window one degree up or down, a long press jumps to the top or bottom, and the centre button returns to the root page. Pattern Velocity has only two range buttons, (15,8) toward the top page and (16,8) toward the lower page, as the next lesson shows.

routes.source_title: Shape accents and rests
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Velocity the range buttons on row 8 differ from Pattern Note, which has three: here there are two, range-up at (15,8), toward the 127-68 page, and range-down at (16,8), toward the 58-0 page.

routes.source_title: Restrict every note to five degrees
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device. The channel range is steps 1-4, the tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Lock all to pentatonic is Off. Lock all to pentatonic forces every note you play onto a five-note subset of the chosen scale, so each scale step below changes which five notes survive.

routes.source_title: Apply Polyperc to the bass channel
routes.caption: Starting point: Channel 2's Device page is open. Read the Device row before changing it.

routes.source_title: Build a four-bar groove with ghost trigs
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped and the norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

routes.source_title: Restart or carry on at a song slot change
routes.caption: A new project with playback stopped and Rate /1. Channel 1 plays range 1-4, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, to its own MIDI output. Channel 2 is not set up yet. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

routes.source_title: Turn chance into explicit rests
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. Every trig has its normal chance of sounding. The Trig params screen is open on its parameter list, showing Fixed Note; no slot is assigned yet. Fixed Note is used here to pin the pitch, so that you hear only which trigs play, not which note.

routes.source_title: Protect playback from a stray tap
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The channel range is steps 1-4, the tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 and the sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Shift press to stop is Off. The Device page for CH01 is showing.

routes.source_title: See what UI motion changes: Off and On
routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major, with the internal clock at 90 BPM and Rate /1. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, UI motion starts Off; later steps turn it On and then change the tempo. This lesson compares the norns screen with UI motion Off and On: Off keeps everything still, On animates the small title pictures and any text too long for its space.

routes.source_title: Quantised pitch: the default and its exceptions
