routes.source_title: Build the recording: Block chords, strummed, then arpeggiated
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1, range 1–16. Set Note MIDI 60, Vel 80, Len 2 steps, Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th; add trigs at 1, 5, 9 and 13 with roots MIDI 60, 57, 65 and 67. Use the Shared channel, Song and grid controls guide for navigation and coordinates.

**Slot 1 — block chords (bar 1).** In Song Editor set slot 1 length to 16. Leave Strum and Arpeggio locks unset. Play the slot, then stop. Check that roots C, A, F and G (MIDI 60, 57, 65 and 67) sound as block triads, with all three notes starting together.

**Slot 2 — speeding strum (bars 2–3).** Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and set slot 2 length to 32. In Trig params assign Chord Note Strum to slot 1, Chord Spread to slot 2 and Chord Accel Mod to slot 3. On steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 lock Strum to 1, Spread to 1 and Acceleration to -1. Play slot 2. Check that each chord’s notes arrive root, third, fifth, with the gaps shortening through the strum.

**Slot 3 — two-note arpeggio (bar 4).** Copy slot 2 to slot 3 and set slot 3 length to 16. Assign Chord Note Arpeggio to slot 4 and lock Arpeggio 1/2 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Arpeggio takes precedence over Strum in this slot. Play slot 3. Check the recorded MIDI event map for the notes of each chord. In C major the four audible pairs are MIDI 60→64, 57→60, 65→69 and 67→71; the fifth is absent.

Play all three slots, then Stop and select slot 1 to restore block chords. The four-bar map is bar 1 block chords, bars 2–3 speeding strum, and bar 4 two-note arpeggio.

routes.source_title: Compare a stored device value with one step-local CC lock
routes.expected_visible_text:
Start with channel 1 routed to the generic CC Device and a four-trig phrase on pattern 1, steps 1–4. This comparison changes the sequenced messages while keeping the instrument’s stored starting value.

1. Tap K1, open PARAMS → MOSAIC and store device CC 1 at 63. Return to Mosaic.
2. Open Channel tasks → Trig params. Select slot 1 with E2, press K2, browse to CC 1 with E3, press K3 to assign it and K2 to return. The slot reads 63.
3. Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 to 99 and release. Play and stop: step 1 sends CC 1 = 99; unmodified steps send 63.
4. Reopen the device’s CC 1 in PARAMS: it still reads 63. Return to the slot, hold step 1 and press K2 to clear the exception. Release, play and stop to restore 63 throughout.

Why it matters: the step lock changes the CC 1 message sent for one note while the stored device default remains 63. A receiver that responds to CC 1 makes the change audible; the MIDI output is the direct check of the values.

routes.source_title: Build the recording: Intro, verse and outro
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major, with playback stopped. If Polyperc 1 or Doubledecker is missing from the Device picker, install and enable the corresponding `nb_polyperc` or `nb_doubledecker` mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 and Doubledecker to channel 2. Give each channel range 1–16.

**Controls and map.** Press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 and K3 to open Device, Masks or Trig params. On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 selects the sound and K3 applies it. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel or Len and E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local value; hold K1 and tap a step to add a trig. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; the column is its position within that group (step 33 is (1,6), step 61 is (13,7)). Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range, then release. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination, release, then tap the destination to edit it. On the length fader, (3,7) gives 13 steps and three taps at (8,7) give 16; (4,7) gives 32 and (7,7) gives 64. In Song Tempo and feel (E1 tasks, E2 task, K3), set Tempo to 90 and press K3. Set each channel Rate /1 on its Clock page and apply with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock; K2 clears a held-step lock. Stop before copying or editing an independent comparison.

**Prepare the two patterns.** On channel 1, create pattern 1 with trigs 1, 5, 9 and 13; set their degrees to 0, 0, 4 and 0. Set channel 1 octave to -1, velocity to 70 and length to half a step. On channel 2, create pattern 2 with trigs 3, 7, 11 and 15; set their degrees to 4, 2, 4 and 6. Set channel 2 octave to 0, velocity to 60 and length to half a step. Checkpoint: in C major the bass is MIDI 48, 48, 55, 48 and the lead is MIDI 67, 64, 67, 71.
**Assign the patterns.** Before arranging, press Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot 1 at (1,2). Select channel 2 at (2,1) and tap pattern slot 2 at (2,2).

**Slot 1 — intro.** In Song Editor set slot 1 length to 16 steps and mute channel 2 with K1 plus its selector (2,1). Check: slot 1 is one bar of bass with the lead muted.

**Slot 2 — verse.** Copy slot 1 to slot 2, set slot 2 length to 32 steps and toggle channel 2 back on. Check: the two-bar verse has both parts; bass remains 48, 48, 55, 48 and lead remains 67, 64, 67, 71.

**Slot 3 — outro.** Copy slot 2 to slot 3 and set slot 3 length to 16 steps. Set channel 2 octave to +1 and channel 1 Velocity to 40. Check: the one-bar outro keeps the same four bass pitches at lower velocity and raises the lead to MIDI 79, 76, 79, 83.

Play the three slots in order, then Stop and select slot 1. The arrangement is intro (bass only), verse (bass and lead), outro (higher lead and softer bass). This is a separate arrangement example; return to the continuing course project when finished.

routes.source_title: Practice longer and shorter Decay envelopes
routes.expected_visible_text:
Comparison purpose: keep the note pattern fixed while only the Decay envelope changes. This recipe has two exercises: compare longer and shorter Decay tails with relative turns, then try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. Use a separate project so neither changes your course arrangement.

Starting point: use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and playback stopped. Make sure n.b. PolyPerc is installed and enabled using [Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b); assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 with range 1–16. In Masks set default velocity 70 and Len ½. Add trig masks on odd steps by holding K1, tapping each odd step and releasing K1. Select Note with E2; for each odd step, hold it and turn E3 to set the absolute MIDI note: step 1=48, 3=55, 5=52, 7=55, 9=48, 11=55, 13=53 and 15=55. Press Channel at (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap Pattern 1 in the second-from-top grid row to assign it before playing; an empty project has no pattern assigned by default.

Controls and step map: press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1, then turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 to highlight Device, Masks, Clock, Trig params or Harmony and K3 to open it. On Device use E2 for the row, E3 for the named sound and K3 to apply. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel, Len or Chd1/Chd2; E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local exception, then release it. To add a trig mask, hold K1, tap that step and release K1. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7. Column is the position within that group. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination and release; then tap the destination to edit it. Set Song Tempo to 90 and each channel Rate to /1, applying changes with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock. K2 clears a held-step lock.

Relative-turn comparison — compare longer and shorter Decay tails while keeping the note pattern fixed. In Song, select slot 1 and set its length to 32 steps with no parameter locks; this is the two-bar straight reference. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and keep slot 2 at 32 steps. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. Open Channel tasks → Trig params and assign Decay to slot 1. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 clockwise by 200 detents; release it. Repeat the 200-detent turn on step 9 and release. Then hold step 5 and turn E3 clockwise by 40 detents; release it. Repeat the 40-detent turn on step 13 and release. Check: steps 1 and 9 form the longer-tail group; steps 5 and 13 form the shorter-tail group, while the note pattern stays fixed. These turns are relative to the current setting; the absolute Decay value shown depends on its starting value and your device. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1 to restore the plain line.

Separate endpoint practice — try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. In Song set slot 1 to 32 steps with no parameter locks. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and set its length to 32. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. Open Channel tasks → Trig params. Use E2 to select parameter slot 1, press K2, use E3 to highlight Decay, press K3 to assign it and K2 to return. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 anticlockwise until the displayed Decay reaches its 0.1 s minimum, then clockwise to the displayed 3.2 s maximum; release the step. Repeat the 3.2 s setting on step 9. Set Decay to 0.1 s on steps 5 and 13, releasing each step afterward. Check the Trig params readout for the long settings on 1 and 9 and short settings on 5 and 13. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1. On your instrument, compare the tails while the notes stay in the same order.

Restore: Select slot 1 to restore the unmodified line. Stop and return to the separate course project when finished.

routes.source_title: Build the recording: Small hours · four bars in C major
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: Use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 and Doubledecker to channel 2. If either player is missing from the Device picker, install and enable its `nb_polyperc` or `nb_doubledecker` mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). Set both channel ranges and Song slot 1 to 64 steps; set Song tempo to 90 and apply Rate /1 on both channels with K3. Check: Song slot 1 shows 64 steps and playback is stopped. Before editing, open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign Pattern 1; select channel 2 at (2,1) and tap (2,2) to assign Pattern 2.

Controls and step map: Open Channel (3,8), select a channel on row 1, use E1 for tasks and E2 to choose Device, Masks or Clock; K3 opens the task. On Masks, E2 chooses Note, Vel, Len, Chd1 or Chd2 and E3 changes the value. Hold K1 while tapping a step to add a trig; hold a step and turn E3 to edit its value. Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range. On Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. Step 33 is (1,6) and step 61 is (13,7). These screens do not page; Pattern Note and Velocity use 16-step pages. Open Song (6,8): slots 1–3 are on row 1; the length fader at (7,7) sets 64 steps.

Checkpoint 1 — bass. On channel 1 set default Note MIDI 48, Vel 70 and Len ½. Add trigs at steps 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41, 45, 49, 53, 57 and 61. Set steps 9, 25, 41 and 57 to MIDI 43; the other bass trigs stay at MIDI 48. Check the Masks readout at one normal step (48) and one low step (43); the bass line now spans all four bars.

Checkpoint 2 — chord layer. On channel 2 set default Note MIDI 60, Vel 45 and Len 3 steps. Set Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th. Add trigs at steps 1, 9, 17, 25, 33, 41, 49 and 57; each chord root stays MIDI 60. Check that the chord tones are the scale third and fifth above each root.

Checkpoint 3 — hear the layer change. Press Play for four bars. Hold K1 and tap channel 2 selector (2,1) to mute the chords; check that the bass remains. Tap (2,1) again with K1 held to restore the chords; check that the same four-bar bass continues under them. Stop playback.

Restore: Leave channel 2 unmuted and playback stopped. Keep this four-bar extension in its separate project; the course Masks phrases use different notes.

routes.source_title: Make one step override a channel Note default, then restore inheritance
routes.expected_visible_text:
1. On Masks, set the channel Note default to G3.
2. Hold step 1 and set its Note to C4; release the step and check that the channel readout returns to G3 while step 1 keeps its exception.
3. Add a D4 exception on step 2, then clear step 1 and finally clear all step exceptions with K1+K2.
Outcome: A held-step Note value overrides the channel default for that step. Clearing exceptions restores the channel Note to G3 across the pattern.

routes.source_title: Build the recording: Average, then Higher
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1, C major and playback stopped. If Polyperc 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable `nb_polyperc` in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1, give it range 1–16 and assign patterns 1 and 2. Turn Lock merged to pent. Off.

Prepare the two-slot comparison with slot 1 selected. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then use E1 for tasks and E2 to choose a task; K3 opens it. In Pattern Trig and Pattern Note, choose patterns from row 1 and edit their steps. On Masks, E2 selects a value row and E3 changes it; hold K1 while tapping a step to add a trig. Open Song (6,8), leave slot 1 selected, and set its length to 32 with the length fader at (4,7). Keep slot 1 selected while preparing both patterns and setting Average. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 only after that setup, as described in step 5. Set Song tempo to 90 in Song tasks → Tempo & feel; set channel Rate to /1 on Clock and apply with K3.

Purpose: compare the same two source patterns under two note-merge rules. Average combines overlapping notes by their mean; Higher adds the range between their highest and lowest values to that mean. Notes from only one pattern should stay the same in both slots.

1. In Pattern Trig, pattern 1, tap steps 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 13. In Pattern Note, set degrees 0, 2, 4, 2, 0 and 4 at those steps.

2. In Pattern Trig, pattern 2, tap steps 1, 5, 9, 11, 13 and 15. In Pattern Note, set degrees 2, 6, 3, 3, 0 and 5. On the Note grid, row 7 is degree 0 and each row above is one degree higher.

3. On channel 1 Masks, leave Note and Trig at X so the patterns supply pitches and trigs. Set Vel to 80 and Len to half a step. These are the recorded channel masks.

4. Open Channel tasks → Merge modes. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until the screen reads ALL. Select Note mode with E2 and turn E3 until the screen reads AVERAGE. Set Song slot 1 length to 32.

5. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2. Keep its length at 32; on Merge modes choose Note mode and set it to UP (Higher). Select slot 1 at (1,1) to return to Average, then play the slots in order. Stop playback when you have heard the comparison.

Listen for: The trig pattern and notes from a single contributing pattern stay the same in both slots. Only notes where the patterns overlap change.

Restore: Select slot 1 for Average. Keep Lock merged to pent. Off and Trig Merge All for this recording, then return to the separate course project.

routes.source_title: Open a filter over two steps
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: Use a stopped four-step channel with trigs on steps 1–4 and a Trig params slot assigned to CC 1 (or the CC that controls your filter). See “Brighten the last note” on Trig Param Locks for slot assignment. The MIDI monitor or the linked event map is the check; no instrument sound is required.

**Make one two-step slide.** Open Trig params and turn E2 to the assigned slot. Hold step 1, turn E3 to 24, release; hold step 3, turn E3 to 96, release. Release all steps and press K3. The cell shows S. Play once: CC 1 leaves 24 at step 1 and reaches 96 as step 3 starts; the captured event map reads 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96. Press Play again to stop.

**Compare local and channel scope.** Hold step 4, turn E3 to 48, and release. This third endpoint distinguishes a slide on step 1 from a channel-wide slide. With no step held, press K3 to turn the channel-wide slide Off. Hold step 1 and press K3; its cell shows S while held. Play: 24 slides toward 96 between steps 1 and 3, then jumps to 48 at step 4. Stop. Check that this is the step-local slide while the channel-wide setting is Off.

**Wrap the channel slide.** Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Wrap param slides On. Release all steps and press K3 to turn the channel-wide slide on again. The step 4 lock now slides back toward 24 across the loop boundary instead of holding at 48. Check the loop-boundary CC values on the monitor/event map.

routes.source_title: Sweep a filter around the loop
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: Use a stopped channel with trigs on steps 1–4 and Wrap param slides Off in PARAMS > MOSAIC. Assign CC 1 (or the CC that controls your filter) to a Trig params slot. Follow the CC 1 event strip in the linked “Carry a slide across the loop boundary” scene or a MIDI monitor.

1. Open Trig params: turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params, and press K3. Press K2, turn E3 to CC 1 (or your filter CC), press K3 to assign it and K2 to return.
2. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24, then release; hold step 3 and turn E3 to 96, then release; hold step 4 and turn E3 to 48, then release. Step 2 has no lock and sends the channel default, 63. Check the four endpoints: 24, 63, 96 and 48.
3. Hold step 4 and press K3 to give that last lock a slide.
4. Press Play and let the loop run. With Wrap Off, CC 1 holds 48 after step 4 and jumps to 24 at the loop point. Stop.
5. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Wrap param slides and turn E3 to On, then play again. At the boundary, CC 1 glides 48 → 40 → 32 → 24 across one step and arrives with the first note. Stop and check the four values in the MIDI strip or monitor.

routes.source_title: Optional probability variation
routes.expected_visible_text:
Starting point: Finish the ghost-note comparison above with ghost trigs on steps 44 and 60. This is an optional, player-run probability exercise, not a reconstruction of the recording. At probability 50, each ghost onset may play or be skipped on each pass, so evaluate the range of outcomes over several loops instead of expecting a fixed recording.

**Set a dependable main beat.** Select channel 1 and open Channel tasks → Trig params. Turn E2 to a slot, press K2, turn E3 to Trig Probability, press K3. With no step held, set the channel default to 100. Check: every main hit remains eligible on every pass.

**Check both boundaries.** On the full Trig Params grid, hold step 44 at (12,6), set its probability to 0, and release. Hold step 60 at (12,7), set it to 0 the same way. Play: neither ghost note sounds in bars 3 or 4; the main hits continue. Stop. Set both ghost steps to 100 and play again: both ghost notes play on every pass, matching the fixed comparison. Stop.

**Try the optional variation.** Set steps 44 and 60 to 50 and play several loops. The musical result to listen for is a quiet pickup that appears on some passes and leaves space on others, while the main hits stay present. Which ghost hit appears can differ each loop; no particular pass or captured result is promised.

Restore the fixed comparison by setting both steps to 100, or remove a lock by holding its step and pressing K2. For a captured 0/100 probability example, see Trig Probability, “Turn chance into explicit rests.”

routes.source_title: Average, then Higher
routes.expected_visible_text: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1, scale C major, playback stopped. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1, range 1-16. Turn Lock merged to pent. Off before comparing, then assign patterns 1 and 2 to channel 1.
routes.expected_purpose: When both patterns trigger on the same step, Note merge chooses the pitch they produce together. Average uses the midpoint of the two pattern pitches; Higher raises that midpoint using the gap between the inputs. Trig merge All combines the triggers from both patterns. Lock merged to pent. is a separate pitch restriction, kept Off here so the comparison isolates the two Note modes.
expected_build_steps: Checkpoint 1 — Pattern 1. In Pattern Trig tap steps 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 13. In Pattern Note set degrees 0, 2, 4, 2, 0 and 4 on those steps. Check the six notes on pattern 1 before you build pattern 2.

Checkpoint 2 — Pattern 2. In Pattern Trig tap steps 1, 5, 9, 11, 13 and 15. In Pattern Note set degrees 2, 6, 3, 3, 0 and 5. On the Note grid, row 7 is degree 0 and each row above is one degree higher. Check that both patterns overlap on 1, 5, 9 and 13, while 3, 7, 11 and 15 belong to only one pattern.

Before merging, verify the overlap: both patterns trigger on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Only one pattern triggers on steps 3, 7, 11 and 15. The comparison changes the shared-step pitches; the single-pattern pitches stay put.

On channel 1 Masks leave Note and Trig at X so the patterns supply pitches and triggers. Set Vel to 80 and Len to half a step. The recorded setup uses these channel masks; it does not leave Vel and Len unset.

Checkpoint 3 — common channel and Average. Open Channel tasks > Merge modes. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until ALL reads. Select Note mode with E2 and turn E3 until AVERAGE reads; these controls apply immediately. Set Song slot 1 length to 32. Check that Strategy reads ALL and Note mode reads AVERAGE before copying the slot.

Checkpoint 4 — compare Higher. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2; keep its length 32. In Merge modes select Note mode with E2 and turn E3 to UP (the Higher comparison). Play both slots, then stop and select slot 1 to restore Average.

routes.source_title: Parameter locks on and off
routes.expected_visible_text: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1, playback stopped. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1, range 1–16. In Masks set default velocity 70 and Len ½; add odd-step trigs and these notes: 1/48,3/55,5/52,7/55,9/48,11/55,13/53,15/55.
routes.expected_purpose: A parameter lock sets a device parameter for one trig only. A Decay lock changes how long that note's sound fades; it does not change the note pattern. In this example, longer Decay locks are on steps 1 and 9; shorter Decay locks are on steps 5 and 13.
expected_build_steps: Slot 1 is two bars (32 steps) with no parameter locks. Keep the eight-note MIDI line unchanged; this is the straight comparison.
Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and keep its length at 32 steps, covering bars 3–4. Open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign Decay to slot 1.

In slot 2, hold step 1 and replay the captured +200-detent E3 gesture, then release the step. Repeat the same +200-detent gesture on step 9 and release it. Check: steps 1 and 9 are the longer-tail group.
Hold step 5 and replay the captured +40-detent E3 gesture, then release the step. Repeat on step 13 and release it. Check: steps 5 and 13 are the shorter-tail group; the note pattern stays fixed.
Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1 to restore the no-lock line. The +200 and +40 turns adjust Decay relative to its current setting; the absolute value shown depends on your device.
Play slots 1 and 2, then Stop and select slot 1 to restore the no-lock line. The note pattern remains the same throughout.

routes.source_title: Choose a trig algorithm
routes.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the third algorithm button (14,2). The five algorithm buttons on row 2 are, from the left: Drum (12,2), a library of classic bass, snare and hi-hat patterns; Tresillo (13,2), a 3-3-2 grouping; Euclidean (14,2), trigs spread as evenly as a mathematical rule allows; Numeric (15,2), patterns from Noise Engineering's Numeric Repetitor; and Rhythm Doctor (16,2). The Trig Algorithm screen marks Euclidean as SELECTED and the fader on grid row 2 lights its third position.

routes.source_title: Create a four-step loop from an empty project
routes.caption: Starting point: a new, empty project, stopped, with Record off. No channel has an output, no pattern has trigs and no masks are set. Tap Channel (3,8): the header reads CH01. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, choose Device with E2 and press K3. Turn E3 one detent to the first output in the list and press K3 to apply it. Whichever name the row shows is fine for this walk-through; in your own project pick the note-capable output you set up in Connect a sound. The Device page for CH01 stays on screen.

routes.source_title: Keep anchors and accent the additions

Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, on steps 1 to 4) is saved as the protected Anchor: its steps always play as written. Pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Add amount is how many additions are admitted and Add accent scales their velocity. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

routes.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. No Trig params slot is assigned yet, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page. Assign slots in two batches; after each Show result, check the last visible CC before continuing.
